generators.lens: Turn the author's idea (one-person and same-image morphs isolate the signal by paired differences inside a host) into a training method: objective, honest claim, one-image and cross-family transfer, and one-person self-morphs at scale.

ideas.name: Self-morph ladder training: signal from pairs, noise from genuine pool
ideas.one_line: Train one network with no second identity: positives are one-person blends (photo with its lossless mirror, or with a second photo of the same person) with exact twins, crossed with storage history; the loss ranks dose inside a host and pins every zero-dose image of every source to one constant score.
ideas.signal: Superposition: two different face images present in one image, seen as doubled fine structure at part contrast. It is the same thing at growing dose in mirror blends, same-person blends and two-person morphs, so the honest claim is 'two captures were mixed', not 'a second person is present'.
ideas.design: Data, per host photo and with no second identity: the photo, the host and its lossless mirror (or the person's second photo) warped to one target shape by the approved warp path (the two halves, zero dose), and their blends made with the engine's own blend line using the mixing fields the alpha-field probe (AF0) verified pixel-identical to the unchanged engine. Left-right uneven fields, mixing fractions below 0.5 and target shapes other than the symmetric mean break the perfect symmetry of mirror blends; an optional symmetric decoy (half of a warp-only image joined to its mirror, zero dose) needs a yes. Every image also passes the existing shrink-and-enlarge call at the registered strengths, and uncovered regions are blanked with one constant colour in all classes. Two variants: the 25,000 SMDD genuine renders only (exactly SelfMAD's training data, so the comparison changes only how self-made positives and their negatives are built) and real photos (FRGC, colorFERET outside the sealed persons, FFHQ); FRLL is never used. Objective with two terms only: a pair term (inside one host, larger measured disagreement must score above smaller, by a margin, with pairs crossing history levels) and a noise term (every zero-dose image of every host, source, history, warp and family is pulled two-sidedly to one constant; the pool also holds photos that never get a blend). No term compares a blend of one host with a genuine image of another, so a file or source property has no term to enter through; the linear version is a matched filter, weight = inverse genuine covariance times mean paired step. Architecture: the MADation recipe unchanged (CLIP ViT-L/14 with LoRA, linear header), one scalar output decides. Test time: one image, one forward pass, one fixed threshold taken from the genuine development pool; no twin, no reference, no gate. The noise term is what carries pairs over to one image: in the GAN first pass the paired win rate is 0.92 but the unpaired AUC 0.78, which under a Gaussian model means about 70% of within-class score spread is a per-host offset that a pair-only loss never touches. Across families the pair term stays inside a family while the noise term pools all pass-through images at one constant, so 'was generated' cannot serve as evidence. Four ablations tie the audit to the method: positives against plain photos only (expected to reproduce the SelfMAD history failure), twins without crossing, twins and crossing with a normal two-class loss, full method.
ideas.controls: Softness: crossed contrast of a softened warp-only image against a native blend of the same host, where the best simple statistic points the wrong way, plus rank correlation of the score with each of the 27 simple statistics inside the genuine pool (at most 0.2 in size). Storage history and warp: FRLL and corrected MAD22 genuine photos native against history-matched at one fixed threshold (at most 10% flagged), photo against warp-only shift at most 0.3 standard deviations. Border: constant-colour blanking of uncovered regions in all classes. Symmetry by-product of the mirror partner: symmetric decoy flag rate and the AUC of the plain mirror-difference statistic on training positives against twins (at most 0.65). Generator fingerprint and capture detail: one-photo reconstruction against photo near 0.5 for families in the pool; FRLL neutral against smiling genuine photos reported without a claim. Second identity is never in training; same-person against two-person is reported dose-matched (idea 3), and tool fingerprint is read by training on the OpenCV-style engine only and testing FaceMorpher, the approved Poisson set and the AMSL and WebMorph cells.
ideas.first_test: Data that exist: the landmark ladder (AR1), 536 hosts, both engines (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img); softened photo and warp-only image of 200 of its hosts at two registered strengths (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/lists/ar1soft.csv); AF0 zero-field images, warped halves and uniform 0.25 and 0.5 blends of 663 other persons (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/img); FRLL and corrected MAD22 genuine photos native and history-matched for scoring only. Features: cached CLIP ViT-L/14 class and mean patch tokens at 224 and DINOv3 ViT-L/16 mean patch tokens at 512 (/mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat, /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat); only the 1,200 softened images may need extraction. Linear heads trained on one-person pairs only (mirror blend against its exact twin, same-person blend against its twin), 5 folds by person: (A) the paired logistic head of the paired-differences experiment (PD1), (B) matched filter with genuine covariance from photos, warp-only and zero-field images, (C) the same with softened copies in the covariance, (T) two-person head as reference, (N) positives against plain photos without twins. Metrics on held-out persons: crossed contrast (softened warp-only at the 61-pixel strength against native two-person morph) beside the best of the 27 statistics; flag rate of history-matched FRLL and MAD22 genuine photos at the native 5% threshold; AF0 zero-field against uniform 0.5 blend (unseen persons, exact twins, two-person morphs never seen in training); unpaired against paired separation. The same heads run on the GAN and diffusion blocks of PD1 for the last metric only. Softened blends do not exist yet, so the crossed test is one-sided for now.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: head (C) below AUC 0.75 on the crossed contrast, or more than 15% of history-matched FRLL genuine photos flagged at the native 5% threshold, or below 0.85 on AF0 zero-field against uniform 0.5; then the one-person signal in these features is softness and the line stops before any fine-tuning. Pass: crossed contrast at least 0.85 with lower bound above 0.75, at most 10% flagged on both history-matched sets, AF0 contrast at least 0.93 and within 0.03 of the two-person head. Sub-claim 'the noise term is worth it' dies if (B) does not beat (A) by 0.03 unpaired AUC in at least two of three families; then a normal two-class loss on the crossed ladder is used.
ideas.sota_path: The SMDD-genuine-only variant is scored on the published tables (FRLL-Morphs, corrected MAD22, MorDIFF) beside SelfMAD and MADation, each release through its own crop with its published number reproduced (own-crop re-score, RS1). The claim is equal or better EER on the landmark cells natively and the lowest false alarms of all detectors on history-matched genuine photos at one fixed threshold; the no-twin ablation is expected to reproduce the SelfMAD failure on the same cells, which joins the audit and the method. Diffusion cells come through idea 2; GAN latent cells are reported under both class policies as a measured limit. Published bars I can cite are only the two in ideas/CONSOLIDATED_v2.md (AMSL 7.26% for MADation ViT-L/14, 3.85% for ViT-B/16).
ideas.compute: First test: up to 0.3 GPU-hours for missing features, CPU heads, about half a day of wall time including review. Full version: ladder build of about 150,000 tool calls plus shrink calls, 2 to 6 hours on 48 cluster CPU cores; about 8 A100-hours per fit (3 million image passes at the speed in the MADation release log, not measured on an A100); two data variants, four ablations, one pre-declared seed plus four for spread (all reported, none picked): about 150 A100-hours, 1.5 days on ten cards.
ideas.risks: Crossing with history may cost native accuracy, because in the landmark first pass the one-person head is only 0.02 above one band-power statistic. The mirror partner may still teach symmetry, which would hit frontal, evenly lit passport-style photos. One-person doses are lower than two-person doses, and the AMSL and WebMorph cells hide ghosting by splicing and retouching. SMDD renders are not camera photos, and target shapes other than the tool's mean must first be verified against the unchanged tool.

ideas.name: Noise-only mirror mix: one-photo positives for diffusion morphs
ideas.one_line: Split the two codes of the diffusion autoencoder: mix only the noise map of a photo with the noise map of its mirror while keeping the photo's own semantic code, use that as the one-photo positive, and use the full two-by-two (plus a fresh-noise render) to decide what a detector reads in a diffusion morph.
ideas.signal: Expected, not measured: fine detail that belongs to two noise maps instead of one capture, the diffusion form of 'two captures were mixed'. The semantic code that carries identity and face layout stays the host's, so the positive has one photo, one identity code and no symmetric face.
ideas.design: A diffusion-autoencoder morph mixes semantic codes linearly and noise maps on the sphere at once, and the record cannot say which one a detector reads. Five renders per host with the unchanged encoder, mixing and render functions: reconstruction (both codes of the host, zero dose), noise-only mix, semantic-only mix, full mix (the published recipe), and a fresh-noise render (host semantic code, new random noise). Partners are the lossless mirror, a second photo of the person, and another person; the semantic-only mix with another person is the second-identity step in isolation. Training use inside idea 1's ladder: zero dose = reconstruction (and the fresh-noise render if it is ruled a one-photo pass-through), positive = noise-only mirror mix at several mixing fractions, with idea 1's objective, architecture and one-image test-time use. The fresh-noise arm matters for the audit: if a head flags it like a mix, then what separates a morph from a reconstruction is that the reconstruction copies its photo too well, and the fair one-photo twin for a diffusion morph is the fresh-noise render. Hosts for fits are FRGC and colorFERET (the 536 hosts of the diffusion generation on Athena, DG1, set B), FRLL is scoring only. Calling the unchanged functions with one code mixed instead of both adds no image operation but needs the lead's yes.
ideas.controls: Simple-statistic floor per contrast (the seven statistics of the frozen-features experiment FZ1 plus the mirror-difference statistic). Equal step count (20), same writer and same size in all arms, as DG1 registers. Reconstruction against photo must stay between 0.45 and 0.55 for the trained head, which separates the mixing trace from the generator fingerprint. Storage history is covered by scoring FRLL arms at the published storage size beside the lossless files. Second identity is isolated by the semantic-only mix with another person and reported, never trained as the main label.
ideas.first_test: Existing images can only kill it. First, the one-person head of the diffusion arm of the paired-differences experiment (PD1; same-person mix against reconstruction, 516 FERET and FRGC hosts, CLIP pooled features, /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/diffae): AUC of two-person morph against reconstruction on held-out hosts and on FRLL at 20 steps. Second, after tonight's full run of the identical-and-mirrored-inputs check (AD1b): do heads trained on two-person morphs rank the 32 mirror mixes above their reconstructions. Third, CPU only, from the codes that run saves (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AD1b/gen/codes_xT.npz when written): is a noise map plain white noise or does it correlate with the photo's own edges. The decisive part needs new renders, not existing data: five extra 20-step renders per host for the 536 hosts of DG1 set B (about 2,700 renders; the inversions are already in that plan), then frozen CLIP and DINOv3 features and a logistic head trained on noise-only mirror mixes against reconstructions, 5 folds by person, tested on full two-person morphs against reconstructions.
ideas.kill_number: Kill on existing data: the PD1 one-person head below AUC 0.60 on two-person morph against reconstruction, or mirror mixes not ranked above their reconstructions (below 0.60). Kill on the decisive part: the head trained on noise-only mirror mixes below 0.70 on full two-person morphs against reconstructions while the head trained on two-person morphs is at 0.90 or more. Pass: at least 0.85, within 0.05 of the two-person head, at least 0.05 above the floor, and reconstruction against photo between 0.45 and 0.55. Reading rules, not kills: if the fresh-noise arm is flagged like the mixes the claim is renamed and the diffusion twin changes; if the semantic-only mix with another person reaches 0.75, identity mixing is readable and idea 1's claim must say so.
ideas.sota_path: MorDIFF and the six DiM cells are in the published tables, and three adapted releases cannot separate a two-person diffusion morph from a one-photo reconstruction (0.40 to 0.49, established). A network trained on noise-only mirror mixes that separates them at 0.85 or more, having never seen a two-person diffusion morph, leads on the column that matters; its native numbers are printed beside under both class policies. The DiM samplers serve as a held-out generator.
ideas.compute: Existing-data part: CPU only, no GPU time beyond PD1. Decisive part: about 1 GPU-hour of renders at the idle-DGX rate plus 0.3 GPU-hours of features, one day including queue. Full: 5,000 hosts (FFHQ, FRGC, colorFERET), two inversions and three renders each, about 40 GPU-hours at the idle-DGX rate (A100 rate not measured), half a day on eight cards.
ideas.risks: The noise map may be close to white noise, so a mixed map equals a fresh one; the idea then turns into the fresh-noise finding, useful for the audit but not a mixing detector. The trace may live in fine detail and die at benchmark storage sizes. A fresh-noise render may be ruled not admissible as a one-photo pass-through. The trace may be specific to this autoencoder and absent in other diffusion morphers.

ideas.name: Dose-matched test and optional head for the second-identity step
ideas.one_line: Compare two-person and same-person blends of the same host at equal measured disagreement; if nothing separates them the paper states that one image shows mixing and not a second person, and if something does it becomes a second, separately declared output.
ideas.signal: Whatever is left of 'two persons' when the amount of mixing is equal: averaged face shape, or structures that do not belong together. Expected to be small.
ideas.design: For each host build the same-person blend at mixing fraction 0.5 and a two-person blend whose fraction is lowered until its measured disagreement inside the face equals that of the same-person blend. Two geometry versions: each blend in its own mean shape (shape averaging stays in, it is a fair identity cue) and both in the host's own shape (texture only). Within-host pairs with the label 'two persons'. If the test passes, the head is a second output on idea 1's backbone, trained only on these pairs, reported as the identity step and never combined with the mixing score. Test time: one image, the same forward pass. If the test fails, no identity output exists and the class definitions gain a split of the third category: single-subject images without mixing (warp-only, reconstruction: trained to score as genuine) and single-subject images with mixing (same-person and mirror blends: flagged by design, listed in their own table, never counted as false alarms or detections).
ideas.controls: Dose matching removes softness and blend strength; the simple statistics must be at chance on the matched pairs and are printed. Same host and the same kind of second photo in both blends (the ladder's composition rule) cancel capture detail and expression. Background and clothing are blanked with a constant colour, because a same-person blend of two sessions ghosts the background like a two-person morph. The exact landmark-shape score is printed beside the head to say how much is shape (0.69 on exact shapes).
ideas.first_test: Existing images: the FaceMorpher graded mixing set (300 hosts, fractions 0 to 0.5 with the partner, /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/fm_graded) and the same hosts' same-person blends (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/facemorpher/R3). Dose proxy on CPU: mean absolute pixel difference to the host's warp-only image inside the landmark hull. Per host pick the graded level closest in dose to the same-person blend. Probe: logistic head on cached CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 mean features, 5 folds by person, two-person at the matched level against same-person, with the best simple statistic beside it. FaceMorpher is the descriptive engine, so the deciding version needs matched uniform fractions built with the OpenCV-style engine through the verified AF0 path (CPU minutes, new images of an approved kind).
ideas.kill_number: Kill: dose-matched AUC below 0.60 with upper bound below 0.65 on both feature sets; then no identity output, and the paper says a single image shows capture mixing only. Pass: at least 0.75 with lower bound above 0.65, at least 0.05 above the simple-statistic floor on the matched pairs, and at least 0.65 in the texture-only geometry.
ideas.sota_path: It does not change benchmark numbers. It makes the claim defensible: one number tells the reader whether any detector of this kind could separate a same-person blend from an attack, and so how the single-subject rows must be read for every detector including ours.
ideas.compute: First test: CPU only, 1 to 2 hours on existing images and cached features. Deciding version: CPU build in minutes plus 0.2 GPU-hours of features. Full version: no extra training run, the head rides on idea 1's fits.
ideas.risks: The pixel-difference proxy may not match dose well; the measured disagreement of the two warped images is better but needs the builds. A pass may be shape averaging only, which an attacker controls through the warp. The sample is small (300 hosts) and the existing graded set is from the descriptive engine.

The warp-only rung of the landmark ladder is not the exact twin of the two-person morph (it is warped toward the same person's shape); exact twins for two-person blends exist only among the alpha-field probe (AF0) images. Mirror blends are separable from two-person morphs by symmetry alone (AUC 1.0, training-free, experiments/AF0/mirror_clip224.json), and the mirror arms planned at mixing fraction 0.5 in the diffusion (DG1) and MIPGAN (AG1) generation jobs will carry this by-product. The exact one-photo reconstruction may be an easy twin for diffusion morphs; a fresh-noise render is another unchanged one-photo run and is in no plan. ideas.name: Layer-count evidence: two superposed textures against one softened texture
ideas.one_line: A pixel-blend morph is two texture layers added, a softened photo is one layer at lower gain; read the number of independent layers with amplitude-normalised fourth-order statistics, train on a scale-free layer-count map, and prove it with a bracketing test (morph must outrank negatives that are sharper AND negatives that are softer).
ideas.signal: The network reads how many independent texture layers a patch holds in the mid bands (1/32 to 1/4 cycles per pixel): adding two unrelated sparse layers divides the excess kurtosis of band-pass responses by N_eff = ((1-a)^2+a^2)^2/((1-a)^4+a^4), which is 2 at 50% mixing and 1 for any single capture. A gain or a compact blur multiplies a narrow band by one number, so the normalised statistic does not move, while softness (energy) does.
ideas.design: Training data: the stored pairs of the blend-evidence probe (AF0) and the SMDD rebuild, made with the unchanged OpenCV-style engine whose wrapper already records both float warped layers. Target per patch: split the partner layer's band response into the part explained by the host layer and the rest, take the two energies e1, e2 after mixing with a(x), and set t = (e1+e2)^2/(e1^2+e2^2) - 1, largest value over three mid bands, zero where the image's own band energy is under a fixed noise floor. By construction t is zero for every one-capture image, zero where the two sources agree, zero where the partner is flat, and unchanged when both layers are softened alike; the registered disagreement targets fail the flat-skin and tone-mismatch checks. Negatives with all-zero maps: both warped halves, photos, zero-field images and the existing softened copies; positives: morphs and their softened copies with the same map. Loss: dense regression plus a within-host bracketed ranking term in which every morph meets its unsoftened half (sharper) and a softened half (softer), and every softened morph meets an unsoftened half, so any monotone function of sharpness wins one pair and loses the other. Architecture: the chosen recipe (CLIP ViT-L/14 with LoRA; frozen DINOv3 tokens for the first pass) with one dense head. Test time: one forward pass on one image, mean of the top tenth of patch predictions in the face box, one score, no band or resolution logic. Predicted pattern across families: strong on landmark blends, silent on GAN latent morphs (one render, one noise draw), and possibly present on diffusion-autoencoder morphs because two nearly orthogonal noise maps are mixed (a guess, the decoder is non-linear). The same three dose points (a = 0, 0.25, 0.5) also tell which law any released detector follows.
ideas.controls: Softness: the bracket of three contrasts (morph against own halves, morph against softened halves, softened morph against unsoftened halves) must keep one sign while Laplacian variance flips. Storage history: R0 against R1 on FRLL and corrected MAD22 per band must stay in 0.45 to 0.55, and warp is checked by R0 against R2w (at most 0.60). Border: all statistics and pooling stay inside the registered face box. Capture detail: neutral against smiling FRLL photo of one person (the noisier files) at most 0.60. Generator fingerprint: camera photo against one-photo reconstruction is reported and only same-generator contrasts are judged. Dose shape separates the two laws (at a = 0.25 the energy loss has reached 75% of its final value, the kurtosis change 36%), and R3 and R3m against R4 per band go to the single-subject table.
ideas.first_test: CPU only, half a day. Images: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/img/{train,val}/{zero,u25,u50,halfA,halfB} and /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/img/soft/{amsl112,fm61}; the landmark ladder /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/{opencv,facemorpher}/{R2w,R3,R3m,R4} with photos in AR1/src, fm_graded, and the softened R0 and R2w of 200 hosts (AF0/lists/ar1soft.csv); FRLL native and history-matched frames from smadcvpr_data/manifests/eval.csv. Features: fourth moment over squared second moment, and mean |c| over root mean c^2, of the responses the registered statistics already compute (Laplacian, Haar HH and LH/HL, noise residual, the seven registered FFT bands) inside the face box, about 22 numbers per image; second line: spread of squared token activations from the cached DINOv3 tokens. Heads: each statistic alone, then a logistic head with 5 folds by person fitted on uniform-0.5 morphs against their halves and scored unchanged on the ladder. Law check: per pair, log(kurtosis of halves / kurtosis of morph) against log N_eff computed from the stored halves. Metrics: the weakest bracket AUC, R0 against R1, the dose share at a = 0.25, and excess over the energy floor of the paired-difference fold (0.912). Secondary: /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a43/gen/{D20,C20,B20}/png256 and GAN roles x1, x2, x3 from /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/gan/items.csv.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: weakest of the three bracket AUCs below 0.65 for the fold head; or every statistic that passes the bracket has R0 against R1 outside 0.40 to 0.60; or the law check has rank correlation below 0.2. Pass: weakest bracket AUC at least 0.75 (lower bound above 0.70), R0 against R1 inside 0.45 to 0.55, R0 against R2w at most 0.60, neutral against smiling at most 0.60, dose share at a = 0.25 below 50%. My expectation is 0.70 to 0.85, about even odds of clearing 0.75.
ideas.sota_path: It changes the target, not the recipe: the round-2 chain (MADation recipe, pipeline-matched and history-crossed SMDD rebuild, warped halves as genuine) stays, and the layer map replaces the measured-disagreement map in the registered five-arm ablation. The state-of-the-art claim sits on the landmark cells, which are pixel blends and keep the evidence in the mid bands at every stored face size (smallest native inter-eye distance 61 px against 132 px in the frame). If the diffusion prediction holds, the MorDIFF cell gets a mixing read that is not a rendering cue. GAN cells are reported as a measured limit.
ideas.compute: First test: 0 GPU-hours, 1 to 3 hours of wall time on the loaded DGX (about 15,000 images). Full version: targets on CPU (30 minutes), dense heads on cached tokens about 1 GPU-hour, five-arm ablation about 2 GPU-hours, LoRA fits 5 seeds x 2 training sets at about 3 A100-hours each = 30 A100-hours, one day on Athena.
ideas.risks: Sensor noise is dense, so a noisy genuine photo looks layered in the fine bands; the mid bands must carry the result. Inside the inner face much mid-band energy is landmark-aligned anatomy, so evidence may sit in brows, hairline and periphery, which splice morphs remove. The invariance is exact for a gain, approximate for a blur inside a band, and false for extended kernels (a double exposure is two layers); JPEG blocks add a weak grid layer. Fourth moments of FFT-band responses need the author's word that an analysis writing no image is not new blur code.

ideas.name: Left-right parity ratio: asymmetry shrinks when two faces average
ideas.one_line: Split the face into mirror-even and mirror-odd parts; symmetric channels cannot change their energy ratio, but mixing two persons averages two unrelated odd parts while the shared anatomy adds coherently, so the ratio falls in the mid bands, in principle for landmark, GAN and diffusion morphs alike.
ideas.signal: The network reads the odd-to-even energy ratio of the face about its midline per band, and in feature space the odd part of the tokens (left token minus mirrored right token) measured against genuine photos only. For a 50% blend the ratio is multiplied by (1+rho_odd)/(1+rho_even): odd parts of two persons are unrelated and even parts are strongly correlated, so it falls toward one half, stays put under any resize or blur, and goes to zero for a mirror self-blend.
ideas.design: Morph-free form: frozen backbone, odd tokens of genuine photos from the 536 ladder hosts (each has a second-session photo), fitted and tested by person folds. The within-person, between-session covariance spans the photo-bound odd part (yaw, light, hair of the day); the between-person covariance spans the person-bound part (nose deviation, brow height, moles). Score: minus the whitened squared length along person-bound odd directions; no morph, tool output or softened image is seen in fitting. Trained form: one network applied to the image and its lossless flip with shared weights; the head sees the even and the odd feature parts separately, so the even part keeps everything the standard recipe has and the odd part is a declared read that no symmetric cue can feed. Test time: one image, its flip, one score. Predictions that can fail: R0 to R1 and R0 to R2w leave both parts unchanged; R2w to R3 halves only the photo-bound part; R3 to R4 halves the person-bound part too; on the GAN ladder x1 to x2 and x2 to x3 map to the same two parts. Look-alike pairing should not weaken it, because fluctuating asymmetry of look-alikes is as unrelated as that of strangers (expected, not measured). Mirror self-morphs and the warp toward the own mirror shape must never be training negatives or positives for this read: they are symmetric by construction.
ideas.controls: Softness and storage history: R0 against R1 per band is 0.50 by algebra, and a miss would point to asymmetric aliasing or border. Border and watermark: face box only, odd-width crop centred on the eye midline, lossless flip (the corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher files carry a one-sided watermark). Expression and capture detail: neutral-only genuine class, and neutral against smiling of one person at most 0.60. Warp: R0 against R2w at most 0.55. Twins: R3 against R4 is the identity read, and R3m is reported as the extreme of the scale in the single-subject table. Generator fingerprint: camera photo against one-photo reconstruction is expected near 0.5 (4-person lead 19.6 against 18.3).
ideas.first_test: CPU only, at most one day, three steps. Step 1 (minutes): split the exact 106-point shapes into symmetric and asymmetric parts with /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AR1/mirror_perm106.json and rerun the landmark arm of the identity-shrinkage triage (/home/narolski/smad-next/src/ID0/iss.py, analyse.py --arm landmark) on the asymmetric part: R0 against R4, R3 against R4, dose, and rank correlation with contributor similarity (cos_HB in /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AR1/pool.csv). Step 2 (about 1 hour): odd and even energy in the seven registered bands inside the face box for the ladder rungs under /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/, the AF0 halves, morphs and softened copies, FRLL native and history-matched frames, /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a43/gen/{D20,C20,B20}/png256 and GAN roles x1, x2, x3 from /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/gan/items.csv. Step 3 (about 1 hour): odd tokens from the cached unflipped tokens /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/{clip224,dinov3_512}/ar1.tokens.npy, centred and whitened on genuine photos only. Heads: the mid-band log-ratio alone, a logistic head on seven log-ratios with person folds, and the whitened token score. Metric: AUC for warp-only against two-person morph, same-person against two-person morph, R0 against R1, and the diffusion and GAN contrasts.

Kill for the generator claim: diffusion 20-step reconstruction against two-person morph below 0.60, or GAN x1 against x3 below 0.55. My expectation: landmark 0.70 to 0.80, diffusion 0.60 to 0.70, exact shapes 0.62 to 0.70.

It supplies a morph-free read with a physical basis that passes the history control, one evidence row that exists for landmark, GAN and diffusion cells alike, and, in the two-view form, a share of the main network's evidence that cannot come from any symmetric benchmark cue. Table numbers stay those of the main recipe, whose full capacity is kept in the even part.

Mirror self-morphs and the warp toward the own mirror shape are symmetric by construction (1.000 separation with no training); the paired-difference landmark head is trained on mirror self-morph against warp-only pairs and may be learning symmetry, which fits its 0.486 on mirror against two-person morphs. On the corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher cell the mirror reads (0.94, and a reversed 0.73) are probably the one-sided watermark noted in the AF0 record, so any frame-level statistic there needs the face box. On FRLL cells the genuine class is half smiling, so "morph less asymmetric" (0.60 to 0.68) is confounded by expression until read on neutral photos only. The same-person diffusion mix in AD1b is a same-session pair, so "a same-person mix keeps its asymmetry" is forced by shared pose, light and hair; the cross-session case exists only on the landmark ladder (R3) and the GAN ladder (x2). Genuine-only fits whose within-person covariance is mostly within-session (identity-shrinkage triage, ID0: 47 of 471 persons with two sessions) overstate every predicted ceiling; the ladder's 536 two-session pairs are the better source.

ideas.name: Three-level ordinal score trained on trace-matched one-person twins
ideas.one_line: One network gives one score ordered genuine < one-person manipulation < two-person morph; the gap between the upper two levels is the second-person reading, measured per family.
ideas.signal: Level 1 reads the trace of each family's mixing operation (pixel superposition, noise-code mixing, code shrink) and, for generators, re-synthesis. Level 2 reads only what a two-person morph has beyond its own one-person twin made by the same operation.
ideas.design: Training images get one of three ordered levels. Level 0 is genuine: camera photos, their softened copies from the existing shrink-and-enlarge path, and warp-only images. Level 1 is one-person manipulation: mirror self-morphs, same-person morphs, generator reconstructions, same-person and mirror mixes of generators, noise-only mixes and spread-matched renders. Level 2 is the two-person morph, and each one has a level-1 twin of the same host and tool. Sources are the SMDD rebuild (SM1) for the published protocol plus the FRGC and colorFERET landmark, GAN and diffusion ladders. The loss is a cumulative-link ordinal loss with one score and two thresholds, a tie penalty for pairs that differ only by softening or warping, and a within-host margin of the morph over its twin. The architecture is the MADation recipe unchanged (CLIP ViT-L/14 with LoRA adapters, one linear head), so only data and loss differ from the comparator. At test time one image gives one score, and benchmark error rates use it for genuine against morph. The single-subject table reports where level-1 images land. The class ruling becomes a threshold choice (lower threshold if same-person morphs count as morphs, upper if only two persons count), with no retraining. Both generator policies are read from the same score: camera photos as genuine, or level 2 against level 1 when reconstructions count as genuine.
ideas.controls: Softness and storage history: photo against its E7 (shrink-and-enlarge) copy, and the E7 flag rate at the threshold that flags 5% of native photos. Warp: photo against warp-only image. Operation trace and generator fingerprint: the two-person morph against its own level-1 twin, where both cancel. Every contrast is printed as excess over the simple-statistic floor, with a kurtosis statistic added to the floor set. Expression and capture detail: neutral-only genuine column, and no conclusion from FRLL neutral-plus-smiling pairs. Border: the same region blanked in both classes.
ideas.first_test: Frozen-feature version on cached data, CPU only. Data: landmark ladder (AR1) patch tokens in /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/dinov3_512/ar1.tokens.npy and CLIP features in /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat/clip224/, with native and E7 genuine photos from the bench_s cache. Features: mean patch token and a centred top-tenth read-out. Heads: an ordinal head (linear and two-layer) with levels {photo, warp-only}, {mirror self-morph, same-person morph}, {two-person morph}, and a binary head (two-person against photo and warp-only) as comparator, with the person folds of PD1 landmark. Metrics on held-out hosts, OpenCV-style engine: AUC two-person against same-person and against mirror, each minus its simple-statistic floor; photo against warp-only; E7 flag rate; two-person against photo. Then a 3 by 3 transfer matrix of the upper-level direction (two-person minus same-person within host) across the landmark, GAN (/mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/gan/feats/clip/G.npz) and diffusion (/mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/diffae/feat/clip/tr.npz) ladders.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: ordinal head two-person vs same-person AUC below 0.75, or less than 0.05 above that contrast's simple-statistic floor, or E7 flag rate above 15% where the binary head stays below it. Pass: at least 0.80 and at least 0.05 above the floor; two-person vs mirror at least 0.80; photo vs warp-only at most 0.60; E7 flag rate at most 15%; two-person vs photo within 0.01 of the binary head. The upper level counts as shared across families only if every off-diagonal transfer cell is at least 0.58 with lower bound above 0.50; I expect 0.52 to 0.60, so a family-specific upper level is the likely outcome.
ideas.sota_path: Under the proposed classes the published tables compare genuine photos with morphs, so level-1 evidence counts and the score keeps what a binary network of the same recipe uses, minus the history cues removed by ties and crossing. I expect table numbers equal to the round-2 protocol arm within seed spread; this is not measured. The ordinal target adds a second-person column that no published detector reports, and one network serves both generator class policies.

Mirror twins are almost symmetric and separable by symmetry alone, and SMDD has one render per identity, so same-person twins must come from FRGC and colorFERET. One ordered axis may cost accuracy if trace and identity evidence are not monotone together. The level of warp-only images and of reconstructions needs the author's ruling.

ideas.name: Code-factorised one-person twins for diffusion and GAN morphs
ideas.one_line: With the unchanged generator, mix only the noise code or only the semantic code, so the one-person twin carries the full mixing trace and the two-person morph differs from it by identity content only.
ideas.signal: It isolates what the frozen probe reads on diffusion-autoencoder morphs: the trace of mixing the noise code (what I expect) or the averaged semantic code. A network trained with these twins at level 1 can call an image a two-person morph only from semantic or identity averaging.
ideas.design: For the diffusion autoencoder, each host A and partner B gets four renders with the same steps and storage: reconstruction (own semantic code, own noise code), noise-only mix (own semantic code, slerp of both noise codes), semantic-only mix (averaged semantic code, own noise code) and the morph. Only the job list changes; encode and render run unchanged, and the codes of the diffusion generation on Athena (DG1) are reused. A face-recognition gate comes before any score: the noise-only mix must verify against A and not against B. For StyleGAN3 the existing spread-matched render already is the trace-matched one-person twin; coarse-layer-only and fine-layer-only midpoints are rendered only if the W+ code statistics fail to explain the image probe. Use one, mechanism: the probe trained on morph against reconstruction scores all four cells. Use two, audit: do released detectors flag a one-person noise-only mix like a morph. Use three, training: the twins become level-1 images of idea 1. Nothing changes at test time: the network trained with these twins still scores one image.
ideas.controls: Generator, step count, storage and host are identical in all four cells, so fingerprint, sampler and storage history cancel exactly. The face-recognition gate proves the twin shows one person. The Laplacian-variance floor is printed for every cell pair, which covers softness. The existing same-person and mirror mixes test the same hypothesis without a new render. For StyleGAN3 the truncated and spread-matched renders give a dose curve in latent spread on one identity.
ideas.first_test: Existing pooled features of four encoders in /mnt/t7/smad_next/FZ1/feats/{clip_mad,clip_native,dinov3,dinov2}/a43.npz, with the probe recipe of /home/narolski/smad-next/src/FZ1/fz1_probe.py, CPU only. Train on two-person morph against reconstruction at 20 steps (B20 vs D20), folds by person, and score the same-person mixes (C20) of held-out persons. Metric one: AUC of C20 vs D20 under the B20-trained probe, with the person bootstrap of the record. Metric two: Spearman correlation of the out-of-fold score of the 200 morphs with the semantic-code distance of their two source photos (/mnt/t7/smad_next/ID0/feat/diffae.npz) and with face-recognition dissimilarity. Also: 20-step to 100-step transfer, the published MorDIFF morphs against reconstructions, the same reads on the 129 FERET and FRGC blocks (/mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/diffae/feat/clip/tr.npz), and the mirror mixes of AD1b when their renders exist. For StyleGAN3: AUC of W+ code statistics from /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/gan/latents.npz against the image probe, and the residual AUC after regressing them out.
ideas.kill_number: Kill (twins not needed for diffusion): C20 vs D20 under the B20-trained probe below 0.70 and correlation with semantic-code distance at least 0.30; the probe then reads semantic or identity averaging and the reconstruction is already the right control. Pass (noise-code trace confirmed, twins needed): at least 0.90 and correlation within plus or minus 0.15. After the renders, the noise-code reading holds if the probe scores noise-only mixes like morphs (AUC against morphs at most 0.60) and semantic-only mixes like reconstructions (at most 0.60). GAN part: no new renders if the residual AUC after regressing code statistics is at most 0.55.
ideas.sota_path: No table number rises from this alone. It decides what may be claimed on MorDIFF-type cells: if the trace is confirmed, a network can ignore the generator fingerprint and still detect these morphs through the mixing trace, and the paper reports the second-person reading against noise-only twins. It also gives the audit a clean figure: one person, flagged like a morph.

ideas.name: Ladder-selected layers and tokens with a fixed nuisance eraser
ideas.one_line: Pick the block and token type where the mixing step is readable above the simple-statistic floor while softening and warping are not; freeze below, remove measured nuisance directions there with a fixed projection, adapt only above.
ideas.signal: Local superposition evidence in patch tokens of a 512-pixel encoder, in the blocks where it exceeds the softness floor. The late class token is used for averageness only.
ideas.design: First measure a profile per block and token type: mixing excess over the simple-statistic floor, warp AUC and E7 flag rate. The junction is the earliest block that is selective. Blocks below the junction stay frozen. At the junction a fixed linear projection removes, from all tokens, the directions spanned by paired interventions: photo against its E7 copy, photo against warp-only image, and expression pairs. It is fitted by least-squares concept erasure on training persons. Above the junction, LoRA adapters and an attention-pooling head over patch tokens are trained with the ordinal loss of idea 1 or the binary loss of the round-2 protocol, on the same history-crossed data. Backbone: CLIP ViT-L/14 at 224 for the published comparison, or DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512 if the profile shows that 224 leaves no excess over softness. Test time: one image, one forward pass, one score; the projection is a constant matrix, not a gate.
ideas.controls: The selectivity rule is itself the softness, storage-history and warp control. After training, a fresh linear probe on the network's last features for photo against E7 copy must stay at or below 0.60 on held-out persons, with an E7 flag rate at or below 10%. An arm without the eraser, with the same data and loss, is the comparator. Region read-outs (inner face, skin, hair outline, background, border) show whether evidence sits in the border or background. Generator fingerprint and capture detail are controlled by the twin contrast and the neutral-only column of idea 1.
ideas.first_test: CPU on cached final-block patch tokens: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/dinov3_512/{ar1,bench_s}.tokens.npy and /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/clip224/{ar1,bench_s}.tokens.npy. Read-outs: mean token, region means, centred tokens with top-tenth pooling, per-dimension standard deviation over patches, mirror difference, and the CLIP class token. Head: the paired linear one-person head and the person folds of PD1 landmark. Metrics on the OpenCV-style engine: warp-only against two-person minus the simple-statistic floor; same-person and mirror against two-person; photo against warp-only; E7 flag rate on FRLL and MAD22 genuine photos at the 5% threshold. Then one extraction pass with hooks (about 12,000 images; class token, mean patch token and five region means for each of 24 blocks) and the same table per block.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: no block and read-out with mixing excess of at least 0.05 (lower bound above 0), photo vs warp-only AUC at most 0.60 and E7 flag rate at most 15%; frozen features then offer no selective read-out and protection must come from the data protocol. Pass: at least one such block and read-out, holding on FaceMorpher and the Poisson set as descriptive checks. The eraser is kept only if it at least halves the E7 flag rate of the no-eraser arm with benchmark error within 0.5 points.
ideas.sota_path: It is the round-2 protocol with a measured choice of where to adapt, so the published comparison (MADation recipe) stays one change away. The frozen part cannot learn storage cues. The record hints at the price: the fully adapted ViT-L/14 release is 3 to 5 points better than the frozen-encoder one on FRLL landmark cells on our frames, and it moves with history.
ideas.compute: First test: 2 to 3 CPU-hours, then about 0.5 GPU-hours for the block profile. Full: eraser arm and plain arm, five seeds each, about 3 A100-hours per CLIP fit, 30 A100-hours; a DINOv3 512 arm about 60 A100-hours; one day of wall time on Athena.
ideas.risks: Linear erasure does not stop the upper blocks from recomputing a nuisance from what is left. Softening is not one direction in token space, so a low-rank eraser may remove little. The selective block may not exist. This is the weakest of the three ideas; its first test is cheap and answers the layer and token question whatever happens.

generators.observations: The brief's range "0.945 to 1.000" includes two-person against same-person mix (0.945), which uses FRLL neutral-plus-smiling files and is confounded; the clean fact is that same-person mixes separate from reconstructions (0.991 to 1.000, unreviewed) as well as two-person morphs do, which argues against an identity reading. Signs disagree across families: landmark morphs lose detail (0.52 times, reviewed), diffusion morphs are sharper than reconstructions (unreviewed), and GAN-trained heads scored diffusion twins below chance (0.26 to 0.32, Codex loop, not reviewed); no experiment tests this directly, and I expect no shared mixing-operation direction. The StyleGAN3 "one-identity render" shows a third person, so morph against render is not a paired contrast; only the spread-matched render shows a contributor. The semantic-code averageness score of the identity-shrinkage triage (ID0) is the only statistic with the wanted ladder profile on two families (0.69 and 0.69, pipeline step 0.50, same-person mix silent) but fails the stored-small control completely (0.000), and in CLIP space the same score reverses sign between landmark (0.364) and diffusion (0.698); all unreviewed. All simple-statistic floors are first or second order, where a mixture and a blur can agree; a scale-free fourth-order statistic (kurtosis of band-pass coefficients) is missing from the floors. The feature caches of the three families use different resize kernels, precisions and frame sizes, so a cross-family test on them is a first look only. The softness floor is higher at 224 px (0.87) than at 512 px (0.76), so a 224-pixel MADation-recipe network has less room to separate superposition from softness. The GAN first pass is one fold with 13 test blocks, and the mirror numbers of AD1b come from 4 persons (its full render folder did not exist at 18:00).

generators.lens: State of the art: strategy for the method that goes into the paper (one network, published tables on FRLL-Morphs, corrected MAD22 and MorDIFF-type cells, ladder controls at one fixed threshold)

ideas.name: Ladder-ordered training of one CLIP ViT-L/14 LoRA network
ideas.one_line: Train the MADation-style network on host ladders from three families so that nuisance rungs are tied to zero score difference and signal rungs must raise the score, on release-style face crops at 224 pixels with one fixed threshold.
ideas.signal: It reads two-capture superposition in landmark morphs and the mixing step in diffusion and GAN morphs, each defined inside one host as the difference between a morph and its own one-capture counterparts (warped halves, warp-only image, one-photo reconstruction). Storage history, warp and softness are defined inside the same host as differences that must be zero.
ideas.design: Backbone: CLIP ViT-L/14 with LoRA rank 2 and a linear head, the registered MADation recipe of the morph-free networks experiment (AD4), last checkpoint, seeds 401 to 405, no selection. Input for training and test: the existing RGB face-detector crop stored as PNG, then the existing loader resize to 224; no aligner (so no aligner border) and no flip averaging. Every training image has a host, a family, a level and a storage state: L0 = photo or SMDD render in any storage state, warp-only image, the morph's own warped halves; L1 = generator run on one photo; L2 = mirror or same-person mix; L3 = two-person morph. Pools: the rebuilt SMDD of the SMDD audit (SM1: balanced partners, halves, shrunk copies) plus mirror rungs; the 663 colorFERET and FRGC persons of the alpha-field probe (AF0; 530 train, 133 for the threshold) with OpenCV-engine, FaceMorpher and, if allowed, Poisson splice morphs; 10,000 FFHQ photos as genuine only; a diffusion-autoencoder ladder and a StyleGAN2/MIPGAN-style ladder generated unchanged on those hosts. Storage crossing: every image exists native and at the registered shrunk strengths, and pairs are formed inside and across storage states in both directions. Loss: cross-entropy on L0 against L3; plus the squared logit difference of every pair of L0 views of one host (weight 1.0); plus softplus(margin minus logit gap) for every lower-to-higher pair of one host (margins 4, 2, 2, 1 logits; weight 0.5). One-photo generator output is either ranked between genuine and morph (policy O, recommended under the three-category class proposal) or tied to its host as genuine (policy A, the stricter fallback); both are trained. Batches are host groups of eight views; 6,250 steps at effective batch 256, constant learning rates 3.33e-6 and 3.33e-5. Test: one image, one forward pass, one threshold fixed at 5% false alarms on every development genuine pool (alpha-field validation persons, SMDD evaluation renders, FFHQ development photos, each in all storage states). Reported: EER per cell on raw benchmark files through the same crop (all 204 and neutral-only genuine photos), miss and false-alarm rates at the fixed threshold on every history-matched, JPEG, blur and stored-small pool, ladder step AUCs on unseen hosts, and a single-subject table. Reference rows with the same recipe: history-only, re-synthesis-only and label-permuted networks. Ablation table: release SMDD, then + balanced rebuild, + halves, + storage crossing, + ladder loss, + camera photos, + diffusion ladder, + GAN ladder, six leave-one-out rows and three left-out-construction rows, five seeds each.
ideas.controls: Softness: softened halves and softened morphs are in training and in test, and warp-only against two-person morph must stay at 0.95 with both softened and at least 0.05 above the best simple statistic on the same images. Storage history: photo against stored photo must be at most 0.60 AUC, shift at most 0.3 standard deviations and false alarms at most 10% at the fixed threshold on every registered pool, including a strength left out of training. Border: the face-detector crop has no aligner border, and benchmark files are scored raw through the same crop. Capture detail and expression: neutral-only genuine column, with FEI and FFHQ as second and third genuine pools. Generator fingerprint: one-photo reconstruction against two-person morph on FRLL and on the MIPGAN controls separates mixing from re-synthesis, policy A removes re-synthesis entirely, and the re-synthesis-only reference network marks the cells it solves alone. Circularity: left-out strength, engine and generator family, and all ladders scored on hosts never trained on (536 landmark-ladder hosts, FRLL, FEI).
ideas.first_test: Data: the alpha-field probe's CLIP ViT-L/14 caches at 224 under /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/clip224/ (lists af0_w1, af0_w2, af0_h, soft, ar1, ar1soft, bench_s), plus 800 softened copies of landmark-ladder two-person morphs made with the verified src/AF0/soften.py. Features: mean-pooled patch tokens, as in the clean-negative test (CN0). Heads: linear, trained on the probe's 530 training persons, five seeds, three arms: label term with photos as genuine; label term with halves, warp-only and softened copies as genuine; the same plus the equality and order terms. Test on the 536 landmark-ladder hosts and on FRLL: AUC of warp-only against two-person morph, native and softened, beside the best simple statistic; paired logit shift from photo to stored photo; false alarms on each FRLL history-matched pool at the development threshold; EER on the FRLL-Morphs and corrected MAD22 landmark cells of bench_s, native and history-matched. CPU only once the running feature queue has finished.
ideas.kill_number: Kill for landmark morphs at 224: softened warp-only against softened two-person morph below 0.90 AUC, or the excess over the best simple statistic with a lower bound at or below 0 (then the signal is softness; go to the canonical-band recipe). Drop only the loss and keep the data protocol if the ladder terms neither halve the photo-to-stored-photo shift nor add 0.02 AUC on softened pairs. Pass: 0.95 or more native and 0.90 or more softened, shift at most 0.3 standard deviations, false alarms at most 10% on every history-matched pool, and EER at most 5% on FRLL-Morphs FaceMorpher and OpenCV against history-matched genuine photos.
ideas.sota_path: Expected (not measured), policy O: FRLL-Morphs FaceMorpher and OpenCV 0.3 to 1.0, WebMorph 3 to 6, MAD22 FaceMorpher 0.2 to 0.8, OpenCV 1.5 to 4, Webmorph 6 to 11, MIPGAN 1 to 6, five-cell MAD22 mean 2.5 to 5.5 against 6.12 published, MorDIFF 0.5 to 3; family-mean miss at the all-pools threshold 10 to 25% against 63 to 87% measured for current detectors. The levers are camera-photo ladders built with the benchmark's own tools for the two clean cells (MAD22 OpenCV and Webmorph), and the re-synthesis plus mixing steps for generator cells. Not reachable honestly on present evidence: AMSL at 1 to 4% (a network that never saw a morph reaches 0.82%; expect 8 to 14%), the FRLL-Morphs five-cell mean of 1.85%, MorDIFF at exactly 0.00, and under policy A the GAN cells (expect 25 to 45%, because mixing alone reads at AUC 0.73 to 0.78). There the paper prints native, history-matched and neutral-only columns, the same-generator step under both class policies, and the morph-free reference rows, and claims only 'best among detectors that pass the storage control'.
ideas.compute: First test: 0 to 0.2 GPU-hours, half a day (CPU on existing caches). Full: about 830 A100-hours over three days in five waves: wave 0 about 75 (crops, features, generator ladders, 10 reference fits, frozen tests); wave 1 about 86 (24 configurations x 3 seeds on ViT-B/16 at 1.2 h each); wave 2 about 145 (6 configurations x 5 seeds on ViT-L/14 at about 3.5 h each, plus a 336-pixel arm), after which ONE configuration is frozen; wave 3 about 405 (14 ablation rows and 9 control and reference rows at 5 seeds); wave 4 about 120 (10 final seeds, one benchmark scoring, reserve). Peak 72 cards. Without Athena: two rented A100 machines run 8 configurations x 2 seeds on ViT-B/16 and 2 x 3 on ViT-L/14.
ideas.risks: The loss needs a host-group sampler and a pair term in the training script; if it slips, the data-only rows still give a network. Only two registered storage strengths exist for camera photos, so the learned invariance may not extend beyond them (measured by the left-out-strength row; the canonical-band recipe removes the question). JPEG history cannot be equalised with allowed operations; only genuine-side JPEG variants exist. Policy O needs the author's class ruling, and transfer from our generators to the published MIPGAN and Greedy-DiM files is not shown.
ideas.evidence: Measured, reviewed: releases move with 61 to 65 px storage and miss 63 to 87% of morphs at an all-pools threshold (experiments/EV1_fixed-threshold-reread/result.md, item 4); a network that never saw a morph reaches AMSL 0.82, WebMorph 0.65, MorDIFF 0.00, but MAD22 OpenCV 31.35 (experiments/AD4/README.md section 5.4; 01_EVIDENCE_DOSSIER.md rows 72, 112); MADation-recipe ViT-L/14 retrains hold under history matching at FaceMorpher 0.4, OpenCV 0.3, AMSL 14.5, WebMorph 7.6, MAD22 OpenCV 8.6, Webmorph 15.8 (docs/sources/methods_table/gather_regular.md row 13; our frames, old MAD22 subset); the ViT-B/16 release reproduces its published regime on the face-detector crop (experiments/RS1_own-crop-rescore/README.md, 17:48); softness floor 0.76 to 0.87 (ideas/CONSOLIDATED_v2.md). UNREVIEWED: clean-negative test, frozen CLIP head 0.9998 cross-tool with 3 to 6% flags on history-matched photos and no statistic floor (experiments/AF0/cn0.json); paired differences, landmark: two-person head 0.980 against a band-power floor of 0.912 (experiments/PD1_signal-isolation-paired-differences/landmark/result.md), GAN mixing 0.73 to 0.78 (same folder, gan/result.md); frozen features read diffusion mixing at 0.945 to 1.000 (experiments/FZ1/result.md). Published values: experiments/RS1_own-crop-rescore/prereg.md; FD-MAD averages docs/PLANNING_RECORD.md line 606 (abstract-level check). Related round-1 idea with one output per rung: ideas/ROUND1_raw.json, pragmatist idea 1.

ideas.name: Canonical-band network at the smallest benchmark storage size
ideas.one_line: Train and test the same network at one fixed small input size, so that every face reaches it at about 63 pixels between the eyes and storage history above that size is absent from the input by construction.
ideas.signal: The same morph signals as recipe 1, read at the inter-eye distance of the smallest benchmark files and of SMDD (61 to 65 pixels). At that fixed size all admissible genuine images have the same sharpness, so a loss of mid-band detail is evidence of blending and no longer a storage cue.
ideas.design: Same backbone, training data, ladder loss, schedule and evaluation as recipe 1. Only change: the loader's existing resize is set to one fixed size S for every image in training and test, with S near 150 (154 = 11 patches or 140 = 10 patches) so that a face-detector crop arrives at about 63 pixels between the eyes. Two forms from existing code: the size flag with interpolated position embeddings, or the loader resize applied twice (to S, then back to 224) to keep the pretrained token grid. There is no per-image measurement and no branch: one size for all images, so it is not a gate. SMDD renders (median inter-eye distance 63.65 pixels, my unreviewed measurement) are then used at native size, without enlargement. Storage crossing stays in training for the 61 to 65 pixel pools at the edge of the band, and one extra arm trains with no storage crossing to show that the invariance comes from the input alone. S is chosen once, from a frozen-feature sweep, as the largest size at which a probe cannot read storage history. Test-time use: one image, one forward pass at size S, the fixed threshold of recipe 1. Reported in addition: the history probe per pool and the false-alarm rate on the existing blurred genuine photos. Ablation rows on top of recipe 1's table: S against 224, with and without storage crossing, and the two forms.
ideas.controls: Storage history: a logistic probe trained to tell a photo from its stored copy must stay at or below 0.60 on every registered pool, for strengths and kernels never used in training, and also in the arm trained without storage crossing. Softness: softened genuine images at or above the band equal the originals after the resize, so that control passes by construction; real blur is the remaining false alarm and is measured on the existing blur variants. Warp-only: warped halves and warp-only images stay in the genuine class, as in recipe 1. Border, capture detail, expression and generator fingerprint: the same controls as recipe 1 (face-detector crop, neutral-only column, FEI and FFHQ pools, reconstruction against morph under both policies). Size ablation: S against 224 on the same data shows what the band costs and what it buys.
ideas.first_test: Data: existing crops only: the landmark ladder's crops (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/crops/main), the own-crop re-score's crops of FRLL photos, of all history-matched pools and of the JPEG, blur and half-size variants (/mnt/t7/smad_next/RS1/crops/), and the earlier corrective crops of the benchmark morphs (/mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a46_corrective_20261108/rgb_clip/). Features: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 mean-pooled tokens at S = 224, 182, 154, 140, 126 and 112, both forms, about 0.5 GPU-hour. Head 1 (history probe): logistic regression, photo against its stored copy, per pool, five folds by person. Head 2 (morph head): warp-only against two-person morph, trained on one tool and tested on the other. Metrics per S: probe AUC per pool; morph-head AUC on the held-out tool; morph-head EER on MAD22 FaceMorpher, MorDIFF and FRLL-Morphs OpenCV against history-matched genuine photos; flag rate on blurred genuine photos.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: no size S with history-probe AUC at most 0.60 on every pool together with morph-head AUC at least 0.95 on the held-out tool. Kill as the main network: at the best S the morph-head AUC is more than 0.03 below its value at 224, or more than 20% of blurred genuine photos are flagged. Pass: such an S exists; S* is the largest one and enters the wave-1 screening as a factor.
ideas.sota_path: Expected (not measured) against recipe 1: equal on MAD22 FaceMorpher, MorDIFF and DiM, which are already at this size; 0 to 2 points worse on FRLL-Morphs FaceMorpher, OpenCV and WebMorph; 1 to 3 points worse on MAD22 OpenCV and Webmorph (about 2 to 6 and 8 to 13). It keeps the fixed-threshold result without relying on learned invariance: false alarms near the nominal 5% on every history-matched pool. It does not rescue AMSL or the GAN cells; the statements of recipe 1 apply there.
ideas.compute: First test: about 0.5 GPU-hour, half a day. Full: about 75 A100-hours beyond recipe 1 (size sweep on ViT-B/16, 15 fits, 12 h; ViT-L/14 fits at 154 pixels take about 1.7 h each; ablation rows about 60 h). Inside waves 1 and 2 the size is one factor of the grid, so no extra wall time.
ideas.risks: CLIP at about 150 pixels is off its pretraining size, and accuracy may drop more than the lost band explains (the resize-twice form is the hedge). The 61 to 65 pixel pools sit at the edge of the band, so a double resize may leave a small trace (fallback S = 126 or 112). 'Softness is evidence at a fixed size' flags real blur and heavy retouching, and that rate must be printed. It needs the author's word that another fixed value of the existing size flag is within the image rules, and images stored below about 60 pixels between the eyes are out of scope.
ideas.evidence: Measured by me today, UNREVIEWED: SMDD genuine renders have a median inter-eye distance of 63.65 px (10th to 90th percentile 59.9 to 65.8; points 38 and 88 of /mnt/t7/Datasety/downloads/SMDD/smdd_bona_landmarks_if106.npz, n = 24,997), consistent with iod_px 63.2 to 64.0 in experiments/SM1_smdd-partner-audit-and-rebuild/pairs_summary_audit.json. Measured, reviewed: registered medians 61.2 (MAD22 FaceMorpher), 63 (DiM), 65 (MorDIFF) and 112 to 254 px for the FRLL-Morphs families; the 61 to 65 px histories move the releases, while 101 to 254 px histories move the ViT-L/14 release by only 0.004 to 0.007 logits, on saturated scores (experiments/EV1_fixed-threshold-reread/result.md items 1 to 3; experiments/AF0/result.md wave 4). Softness separates a morph from its halves better at 224 than at 512 (0.87 against 0.76; ideas/CONSOLIDATED_v2.md). Estimate, not measured: a face crop at 224 has about 95 px between the eyes. Related round-1 idea, blocked then by the resampling rule: 'one network at the common Nyquist' (ideas/ROUND1_raw.json, physics lens).

ideas.name: SMDD-Ladder: three-family ladder built only from SMDD renders
ideas.one_line: Train the same network only on images derived from SMDD renders (landmark rebuild, mirror rungs, diffusion and GAN generators run on the renders), so the row is comparable with the field, every camera-photo pool is held out, and the set can be released.
ideas.signal: The same signals as recipe 1, learned from synthetic identities only: superposition against the morph's own warped halves, and the mixing step against one-render reconstructions and mirror mixes. The open question it tests is whether these signals carry from renders to camera photos.
ideas.design: Hosts: the 25,000 genuine renders of the SMDD training split; nothing else enters training. Landmark family: the rebuild of the SMDD audit (SM1) with balanced partners, both warped halves and mirror warp-only images as genuine, and the mirror self-morph as the one-person rung. Diffusion family: the pinned diffusion autoencoder run unchanged on 6,000 to 25,000 renders: reconstruction, mix with the mirror image, two-render mix, at 20 steps with a 100-step subset. GAN family: the existing StyleGAN2 inversion and MIPGAN-style code run unchanged on the renders: inversion output, mirror-code mix, latent-mean and optimised two-render morphs. Storage: native and the registered shrunk copy for every image. Objective, backbone, crop, schedule and evaluation as recipe 1, preferably at the small size of recipe 2, where SMDD is at native size. Test-time use: one image, one forward pass, one threshold fixed on SMDD evaluation-split renders and FFHQ development photos. All camera-photo ladders (536 landmark-ladder hosts, FRLL, FEI) and all benchmarks are unseen sources. The set is published and shared with the SMDD authors, as their terms require. Ablation rows: release SMDD, + balanced rebuild, + halves, + storage crossing, + ladder loss, + diffusion rungs, + GAN rungs, mirror rung removed.
ideas.controls: All controls of recipe 1 apply, and every camera-photo ladder is an unseen source, which answers 'trained on the ladder, passed the ladder'. Softness and warp: halves, mirror warp-only images and shrunk copies are genuine in training, and the softened-pair mark of recipe 1 is read on camera-photo ladders. Generator fingerprint: under policy A the reconstruction of a render is tied to the render, and reconstruction against camera photo must stay at or below 0.65 AUC. Mirror symmetry: the mirror rung carries no label and is ranked below two-render morphs, and a row without it shows it is not the carrier. Partner structure: balanced partners, each render a partner at most twice.
ideas.first_test: The landmark half is already under test in the SMDD audit's rebuild arms on frozen features (SM1, part 3). Proxy for the generator half on existing data: train a mixing head (frozen CLIP ViT-L/14, mean-pooled, logistic) on the existing diffusion blocks of colorFERET and FRGC persons under /mnt/t7/smad_research/diffae-expanded123-v1/run/ (102 blocks: reconstructions, same-person mixes, two-person morphs). Test it on the FRLL arms of the earlier MorDIFF controls (features under /mnt/t7/smad_next/FZ1/): two-person morph against reconstruction at 20 steps, and published MorDIFF against reconstructions. Render-to-photo test, about 1 GPU-hour of new generation from existing renders: the diffusion autoencoder on 600 SMDD renders (reconstruction, mirror mix, 300 two-render mixes), the same head, the same FRLL test. Metric: AUC with person bootstrap, and reconstruction against camera photo for the same head.
ideas.kill_number: Kill the generator rungs of this protocol if the render-trained head is below 0.80 AUC on FRLL two-person morph against reconstruction at 20 steps (the in-pool probe is at 0.987, unreviewed), or if the proxy trained on other camera pools is below 0.85. Under policy A also kill if that head separates reconstruction from camera photo above 0.65. Pass: 0.90 or more; then generate the full set.
ideas.sota_path: Expected (not measured), policy O: FRLL-Morphs FaceMorpher and OpenCV 0.5 to 2, WebMorph 5 to 9, AMSL 10 to 16; MAD22 FaceMorpher 0.3 to 1, OpenCV 5 to 9, Webmorph 12 to 17; MorDIFF 1 to 5; GAN cells 2 to 8 (25 to 45 under policy A). That is at or above the published MADation level on most cells with the storage control passed, but not the best number on MAD22 OpenCV (2.23) or FRLL-Morphs WebMorph (3.42). Its role is the comparable row and the released set; it becomes the headline if it is within 2 points of the camera-photo protocol on the clean cells.
ideas.compute: First test: 0 GPU-hours for the proxy and about 1 GPU-hour for the render-to-photo test; half a day. Full: about 150 A100-hours (generation 40 to 60, with encodes estimated at 5 s per render on an A100, to be measured; five-seed rows at two sizes 35; extra ablation rows 55). Morph builds and crops stay on CPU machines, not on Athena.
ideas.risks: The step from renders to camera photos may break the mixing head. 256-pixel sources hold no fine detail, so the clean high-resolution cells (MAD22 OpenCV, Webmorph) will lag the camera-photo protocol. The mirror rung is a symmetric face and must not be the only one-person rung. Whether the StyleGAN2 inversion code runs on Athena is not verified, and the origin of the SMDD morph-source folders on disk is not recorded.
ideas.evidence: Measured, reviewed: SMDD's 15,000 training morphs share five second contributors and no genuine render is a contributor (experiments/SM1_smdd-partner-audit-and-rebuild/result.md, part 1); SMDD-trained MADation-recipe retrains hold under history matching on landmark cells (docs/sources/methods_table/gather_regular.md row 13). UNREVIEWED: frozen-feature probes read diffusion mixing at 0.945 to 1.000 inside FRLL (experiments/FZ1/result.md); a mirrored photo is as far from the photo as a second photo of the same person in the diffusion autoencoder's semantic code, 0.776 against 0.773, four persons (experiments/AD1b/result.md); my measurement of SMDD's inter-eye distance (63.65 px, see recipe 2). Timings: experiments/DG1_diffusion-generation-athena/result.md and experiments/AG1/result.md. SMDD terms and the author's acceptance: 07_DECISIONS_NEEDED.md. From the old record, not re-verified: a 74-pair frozen head reached 0.947 on held-out FRGC dyads (ideas/ROUND1_raw.json, pragmatist idea 1).

generators.observations: SMDD genuine renders have a median inter-eye distance of 63.65 pixels (my light read of the stored landmarks, unreviewed), the same size as the three small-storage benchmark families (61 to 65), which may explain why exactly those histories move SMDD-trained detectors. The MADation-recipe ViT-L/14 retrains sit at 0.3% on FRLL-Morphs OpenCV but at 8.6% on MAD22 OpenCV (same tool, same persons), and history matching leaves our aligner's border in place, so 'CLIP rows hold on landmark cells' should wait for the own-crop re-score (RS1). History matching does not equalise compression: AMSL is separated perfectly by JPEG quality and no allowed operation tests the morph side. The Athena diffusion set B (DG1) is built on the landmark ladder's 536 hosts; if it enters training, that ladder is no longer person-held-out for our network. The clean-negative test (CN0) has an empty cue list, so its 'mixed' verdict comes from a missing statistic floor, not from a result. Our SMDD-only ViT-L/14 retrains reach 0.8% on MAD22 MIPGAN-I where the release publishes 20.32%, so GAN-cell numbers are pipeline-dependent and no control explains the gap. The morph-free networks experiment (AD4) scores with flip averaging while the releases are read without it; under 'no fusion of scores' every headline row should be without it. The softened evaluation copies of the landmark ladder cover photos and warp-only images but not two-person morphs, so the softness control has one side only.

generators.lens: Nuisance: training and model constraints under which the measured cues cannot help, each verified with the ladder. Three senses of "cannot help", one idea per sense: the cue cannot cause a flag (idea 1), the cue is not rewarded in training (idea 2), the cue is not in the input (idea 3).

ideas.name: Training with a false-alarm limit for every storage history
ideas.one_line: Train the MADation recipe (CLIP with LoRA, low-rank adaptation) so that at the network's own 0.5 rule no kind of genuine image (source pool by storage history) is flagged more than 1% of the time, and prove it on doses, processes and photo pools left out of training.
ideas.signal: It reads the same signal as the base recipe: the trace of mixing two captures (double contours and superposed textures in landmark morphs, the code-mixing trace where generator ladders are in training). It adds no new signal; it fixes where genuine scores may sit, so storage history, resampling softness and warp without blending cannot cause a flag.
ideas.design: Training images hold no FRLL, FFHQ or FEI person: the rebuilt SMDD arms (balanced partners, warped halves, shrunk copies; SMDD rebuild, SM1) and the FRGC and colorFERET landmark material of the alpha-field probe (AF0), with softened copies made only through the existing shrink-and-enlarge path. Genuine images are grouped into environments, source pool by state (as stored; shrink path at each strength; warp-only or half; half then shrink), split by expression where labelled, and every batch draws equally from them. The strengths form a grid between 0.36 and 1.0 of what a 224 input can carry (registered targets 61.2 and 112.7 px for 512 frames; scales 0.75 and 0.5 beside 0.3125 for SMDD renders, which needs the author's yes), because today's training doses (1.0 and 0.36) do not include the benchmark's dose (about 0.7; my arithmetic). Morphs carry histories on both sides of the blend (morph then shrink; shrink the sources then morph). Objective: the usual loss on morphs, and for each genuine environment a margin loss with its own weight, raised every few hundred steps while more than 1% of that environment's held-out training-pool images score above logit 0 (lowest miss subject to a false-alarm limit per environment). The architecture is the unchanged MADation recipe (CLIP ViT-L/14, LoRA, linear header); training length, last checkpoint and seed list are fixed in advance and nothing is selected on a benchmark. At test time one image gives one logit and is flagged if it is above 0; no threshold is fitted on any test pool, and EER and AUC are printed as well. An optional arm adds a one-sided hinge on photo and processed-copy pairs; it is not core because the earlier consistency loss (A49) failed. Cost expected, not measured: at most 1 to 2 EER points on landmark cells, while diffusion and GAN cells fall to what the generator ladders teach, because the limit creates no signal.
ideas.controls: Storage history: at the own rule, flag rates of R0, of R1 for every family's history pool and of three kinds of left-out environment (an unused dose, the existing JPEG 50, blur and 50% resample files, and the unseen pools FRLL, FFHQ and FEI) must each be at most 5% with an upper bound of at most 10%. Softness: softened photos and softened warp-only images are protected environments, and two-person against same-person morphs (R4 against R3, equal softness by PNG size, AUC 0.51, unreviewed) is printed as the softness-free contrast. Border: the decisive read uses the same constant-colour blanking in both classes. Capture detail and expression: environments are split by pool and expression, the headline uses neutral-only FRLL photos, and pools never trained on are rows of the table. Generator fingerprint: one-photo reconstructions are their own environment and are printed under both class policies. The mirror rung is not used as a negative, because a 32-pixel thumbnail separates it from two-person morphs at 0.93 (unreviewed).
ideas.first_test: Fixed-rule head test (NU1): frozen features, logistic heads, 5 folds by person. Features: DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512, mean patch tokens in /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat/dinov3_512/af0_{ar1,af0_w1,af0_w2,bench_s}_mean.npz (decides) and CLIP ViT-L/14 at 224 tokens in /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/clip224/ (beside), with new extraction only of files that exist: the 1,200 softened images of /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/lists/ar1soft.csv and the 612 FRLL genuine frames of variants jpeg50, blur1 and resample50 in /home/narolski/mambamorph-code/smadcvpr_data/manifests/eval.csv. ideas.kill_number: Kill: head C flags more than 10% of any left-out pool of at least 200 images while its training environments are at or below 2% (the limit does not transfer), or its family-mean miss on the seven landmark cells is not at least 3 points below head X at the matched post hoc threshold (the objective adds nothing over crossed data plus a worst-pool threshold). Pass: worst left-out pool at most 10% (point value at most 5%) and miss at least 3 points below matched X, or family-mean miss at most 5%.
ideas.sota_path: The recipe it constrains is already near zero miss on FRLL landmark cells at one fixed threshold (ViT-L/14 recipe retrains: 0.02 to 0.3% at the development threshold, 4 to 22% when every pool is protected; my unreviewed read), so the aim is to keep those numbers and close the gap between the two. The headline table is flag and miss rates at each detector's own rule, where the releases fail (SelfMAD flags 0 / 45 / 55 to 79 / 97% of genuine photos) and ours is held to 5%. EER on the published cells is printed beside, with our own retrains as the bar on our frames. Diffusion and GAN cells improve only as far as the generator ladders in training carry, and are printed under both class policies.
