ideas.name: Train only on what the measured cues cannot explain
ideas.one_line: Turn the audit's cue table into a frozen cue model, add its log-odds to the detector's logit during training only, and score with the detector alone, so that nothing the measured cues explain is rewarded.
ideas.signal: It reads evidence of mixing that the cue vector does not carry: double contours, a second face's structure, texture from two captures. By construction the training reward does not come from sharpness, band power, colour, border, file size, pool, history dose, partner or smile.
ideas.design: The cue vector of a training image is measured with existing unchanged code: the 26 statistics of cue_floor.stats, PNG size, six colour statistics, zero-border share, the geometry smile probability of the SMDD rebuild, and labels known by construction (pool, tool, history dose, partner). A cue model (gradient-boosted trees) predicts the label from the cue vector and is fitted in folds by person, so every training image gets an out-of-fold, calibrated log-odds b(x). Overlap rule: the cue model's out-of-fold AUC on the training set must lie between 0.6 and 0.9, and above 0.95 more crossed data are added first (dose grid, histories on both sides of the blend, balanced partners), which replaces the one-number acceptance of the rebuild. The detector is the unchanged MADation recipe with loss cross-entropy of sigmoid(f(x) + b(x)); at test time only f(x) is computed, so the cue model never sees a test image and there is no fusion. If b is the true log-odds given the cues, no function of the cues alone lowers the loss, and the gradient is near zero where the cues already decide, so the fit is driven by soft genuine images and sharp morphs. It is the only lever for cues we may not or cannot equalise by an image operation (colour, capture detail, expression, partner, pool). The operating point comes from idea 1's limit or from one threshold on a crossed development pool. A cheaper comparison arm uses the usual loss with overlap weights from the same cue model. Cost expected, not measured: cells that cues solve get worse, and the table prints per cell the price (native EER of the residual fit minus the usual fit on the same data) beside the same difference on the history-matched column.
ideas.controls: Softness and storage history: among genuine photos of one unseen pool the largest absolute rank correlation between the score and any cue must be at most 0.2, and flag rates on R0, R1 and R2w are read at one fixed rule. Signal beyond cues: the AUC of warp-only against two-person morphs within fifths of the cue log-odds, and two-person against same-person morphs (R4 against R3), the rung where softness is equal by measurement. Border, capture detail and expression: border share, file size, backdrop statistics and smile probability are columns of the cue vector, and the read uses neutral-only FRLL photos with common blanking. Generator fingerprint and partners: an is-a-render label and the partner label are columns, so release morphs with the five partners give no gradient. Planted cue: with a constant-colour corner mark on 80% of morphs and 20% of genuine images, the usual loss must pick it up and the residual fit must not (gap between agreeing and reversed test sets at most 0.03). Leaving one cue family out of the cue vector and repeating the correlation read states how far the protection reaches beyond listed cues.
ideas.first_test: Cue-residual head test (NU2): no new image and no GPU. Data: ladder R0, R2w, R3 and R4 of the 536 hosts, OpenCV-style engine, under /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/, and the FRLL and MAD22 landmark cells with native and history-matched genuine photos from the bench_s list. Features: /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat/dinov3_512/af0_ar1_mean.npz and af0_bench_s_mean.npz (DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512, mean patch token), with CLIP mean patch tokens from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/clip224/ beside. Cues: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/ar1.npz and bench_s.npz (26 statistics and PNG size per image). Heads: logistic, 5 folds by person with partner-safe folds, contrast R4 against R0 and R2w, three arms: usual loss, overlap-weighted, residual (offset = cue model fitted inside the training folds). Metrics on held-out hosts and FRLL: largest absolute rank correlation of the score with any cue among genuine photos, cue-conditional AUC of R2w against R4, AUC of R3 against R4, share of history-matched FRLL photos flagged at the threshold that flags 5% of native ones, and EER on the seven landmark cells. If the usual-loss head already shows a cue correlation below 0.3 and flags at most 10%, the decisive test is one pair of LoRA fits of the ViT-B/16 recipe on Athena (usual against residual), read on the rise under history matching on the seven diffusion cells.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: the usual-loss head has a cue correlation of at least 0.3 and the residual head does not at least halve it; or the residual head's cue-conditional AUC is below 0.70; or its held-out-tool AUC drops by more than 0.05; in the LoRA version, the residual fit's rise under history matching is more than half of the usual fit's (reference in the record: +11.4 points). Pass: cue correlation at most 0.2 on FRLL genuine photos, cue-conditional AUC at least 0.80, and every history-matched pool at most 10% flagged.
ideas.sota_path: It is a change of loss on the recipe that already leads on landmark cells, so backbone, data and the controlled comparison with MADation stay. Where its price column is near zero, the published number stands with a proof that the measured cues did not earn it. Where the price is large the cell was cue-solved, and the paper says so with the morph-free row beside it. Combined with idea 1 it gives one network with a fixed rule.
ideas.compute: First test: 0 GPU-hours (features and cue statistics exist), under 1 CPU-hour, 1 to 2 hours wall. Full: cue statistics for about 100,000 training images (about 8 core-hours, my estimate), 5 residual fits of CLIP ViT-L/14 (about 18 A100-hours; the usual-loss arm is shared with idea 1) and the planted-cue pair on ViT-B/16 (about 5 A100-hours): about 25 GPU-hours, one day.
ideas.risks: After crossing the data, the residual loss may add nothing over the usual loss. If the cues explain almost everything (floor 0.91 for warp-only against two-person, unreviewed), few images drive the fit and seeds will spread. The protection covers listed cues only. The technique is known from language tasks (product of experts, residual fitting; cited from memory, no paper opened), so the claim is the audited bias model, not the loss.
ideas.evidence: From the reviewed record: SMDD classes separate by one sharpness number at AUC 0.99 or more (/home/narolski/smad-next/08_CUE_MATRIX.md rows 11b and 19); a network with no morph in training reaches 2.6% EER or better on 9 to 10 of 12 scored cells (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/EV1_fixed-threshold-reread/README.md section 8); the 0.52 Laplacian ratio and the 0.76-0.87 floor (/home/narolski/smad-next/ideas/CONSOLIDATED_v2.md); rise of +11.39 points under history matching for eight ViT-B/16 recipe retrains (earlier record, quoted in /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/SM1_smdd-partner-audit-and-rebuild/prereg.md). UNREVIEWED leads: simple-statistic floor 0.91 and excess 0.02-0.07 for frozen heads (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/PD1_signal-isolation-paired-differences/landmark/result.md, one fold); equal PNG size of same-person and two-person morphs (AUC 0.51) and probes at 0.86-0.93 (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AR1/baselines.json and gate_c.json, my read, experiment still running). Existing inputs: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/, /home/narolski/smad-next/src/C_cue_checks/c_checks.py, /home/narolski/smad-next/src/SM1/expr_geom.py. Not verified: that these scripts run unchanged on every training pool.

ideas.name: Canonical view: one storage band and frame for every input
ideas.one_line: Run the existing shrink-and-enlarge path with one fixed target on every image, at training and at test, and blank the same frame region in every image, so that storage history above the band and the border are not in the network's input at all.
ideas.signal: It reads what survives at the benchmark's own lowest storage band (inter-eye distance about 61 px): contours doubled by more than a few pixels, coarse double structure and how average the face is. It cannot read fine softness, storage history above the band, a JPEG grid or the border, because no input contains them.
ideas.design: Front end T is the same code path for every image and makes no decision: the unchanged alignment, then the existing shrink path with scale = tau / native inter-eye distance (the registered history-matching branch with one constant in place of the family median), then constant-colour blanking outside one fixed mask. tau is 61.2 px first (a registered strength), and a second arm uses 48 px because inputs natively at 61 to 70 px otherwise pass almost unchanged. The network is the unchanged MADation recipe on T(x), trained on the crossed SMDD rebuild and the landmark material after T. Certificate part a: the strongest probes we have (frozen CLIP and DINOv3 patch tokens, a small network from scratch, a LoRA fit) must not separate T(R0) from T(R1) on held-out persons. Certificate part b: the network with no morph in training, refitted on T(render) against T(shrunk render), must be at chance on its own task and on every cell. Certificate part c: border share separates nothing, because the mask is identical. If the band costs too much on splice-type families, a second network sees the native image and is anchored to the canonical one: usual loss on morphs, and on genuine images its score may not exceed the canonical network's score of T(x) by more than a margin. Both versions use one network and one image at test time. Not removed: softness inside the band, capture detail inside the band, expression, the low-frequency part of a generator fingerprint and partners, which ideas 1 and 2 handle. Running the path on benchmark files at test time is a new scope and needs the author's yes. Cost is not known: both-class resampling at 50% costs the recipe nothing on FRLL landmark cells, but 61 px turns the mean 4.2 px misalignment into about 1.3 px, so losses on AMSL and WebMorph are expected.
ideas.controls: Storage history and softness above the band: probe AUC of T(R0) against T(R1) at most 0.55, and the no-morph network at chance on canonical inputs. Softness inside the band: T(R2w) against T(R4) is printed beside the simple-statistic floor measured at the band, with R3 against R4 beside it. Border and background: the constant-colour mask is identical, so border share AUC is exactly 0.5 for any reader. Route check on existing files: a photo stored small (arm E of the MorDIFF ladder study, A43) against the history-matched pool in the same frame, two genuine routes to the same band. Capture detail, expression and generator fingerprint inside the band are not controlled by this idea and are read with neutral-only photos, unseen pools and one-photo reconstructions as in idea 1.
ideas.first_test: Canonical-view test (NU3): existing data plus about 1,300 shrink-path copies of our own ladder images (the scope approved for the softened-examples wave of the alpha-field probe, AF0), CPU minutes. Existing: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/img/soft/fm61 and soft/amsl112 (61.2 and 112.7 px copies of R0 and R2w for 200 ladder hosts), and corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher morphs (native median 61.2 px) against the 204 history-matched genuine frames in /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/mad22_canonical_E7_inputs_v3_20261109T113746Z/e7/FaceMorpher (features in the bench_s list). To build with the unchanged path: 61.2 px copies of the 536 OpenCV-style R4 morphs in /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/opencv/R4, of R2w for the other 336 hosts, and of the 200 existing 112.7 px copies of R0 (a second pass). Features: DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512 and CLIP ViT-L/14 at 224, mean patch token; heads: logistic, 5 folds by person. Reads: (a) probe AUC of T(R0) against T(R1 at 112.7 px); (b) AUC of T(R2w) against T(R4) beside the native value and the simple-statistic floor at the band; (c) EER on MAD22 FaceMorpher at the band for the head trained on canonical ladder images; (d) the route check on the A43 files.
ideas.kill_number: Kill: read (a) above 0.65 (the history is still in the input), or read (b) below 0.85 or within 0.05 of the simple-statistic floor, or read (c) above 10% EER. Pass: (a) at most 0.55 with an upper bound of at most 0.60, (b) at least 0.95 and at least 0.05 above the floor, (c) at most 5%.
ideas.sota_path: On published tables the network is scored on the native files, because T is part of the network. On the 8 of 17 cells whose morph files are already at the band nothing is lost on the morph side. On the other landmark cells the cost test decides between the canonical network and the anchored network that also sees the native image. If both lose more than 3 points on two or more landmark cells, the idea is kept as an instrument (a canonical-band column for every detector), not as the method.
ideas.compute: First test: 20 to 30 CPU-minutes for the copies, about 0.3 GPU-hours of features, 3 to 4 hours wall. Full: T on about 100,000 training images (about 28 core-hours, my estimate), 5 fits (about 18 A100-hours), the no-morph control (5 ViT-B/16 fits, about 6), the anchored arm (about 18): about 45 GPU-hours, 1.5 days.
ideas.risks: The band may delete the evidence for splice-type morphs (AMSL, WebMorph). Inputs natively at 61 to 70 px get almost no shrink, so their route may stay readable; the 48 px arm and the route check test this. Running the path on benchmark files at test time needs the author's yes. The scale uses the detected eye distance, which is a normalisation like alignment and not a gate, but a reviewer may object.
ideas.evidence: Reviewed: storage history moves released detectors, and the border our aligner leaves separates 11 of 12 scored cells (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/reviews/REVIEW_EV1_20261111.md; EV1 README); a network with no morph reaches 0.00% on MorDIFF (/home/narolski/smad-next/01_EVIDENCE_DOSSIER.md, A47 I-3). Registered targets: 61.2 px in /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/mad22_canonical_E7_inputs_v3_20261109T113746Z/family_native_ied_targets.json and 112.7 px in /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AF0/result.md, where the path was verified bit for bit. My UNREVIEWED read: both-class 50% resample or blur leaves FRLL landmark AUC unchanged for the recipe retrains and the ViT-L/14 release (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/EV1_fixed-threshold-reread/A3_crossed.csv). From the round-2 vetting, NOT opened at primary: frozen CLIP patch tokens read history at AUC 1.0 and per-image normalisation does not remove it; forensics reviewer's measurements (mean landmark displacement 4.19 px; Laplacian variance photo 187.7, half 72-78, morph 39.2) in /home/narolski/smad-next/ideas/ROUND2_vetting_raw.json. All cost statements are expectations, not measurements.

vetting.lens: Paired differences as a training method

cards.name: Self-morph ladder training: signal from pairs, noise from genuine pool
cards.one_line: Add one-person blends with exact warp-only twins and crossed storage history as extra arms of the registered SMDD rebuild (SM1) on the unchanged MADation recipe and loss; the mirror partner and the pair-plus-noise loss stay only if they pass their own tests.
cards.novelty: Closest work found. SelfMAD (FG 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05504): positives made from genuine images only by blending an image with a transformed copy of itself; same premise (pipeline details from a third-party summary, full text not read). Self-blended images (CVPR 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.08376; abstract only, so whether a mirrored partner or unblended transformed negatives occur is NOT verified). Selfmorphs labelled genuine: MorDeephy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03110), MorphGuard (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10497), from search summaries. Single-center loss (CVPR 2021, https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Li_Frequency-Aware_Discriminative_Feature_Learning_Supervised_by_Single-Center_Loss_for_Face_CVPR_2021_paper.html) pulls genuine faces to one centre: this is the noise term; its linear form is LDA. Aligned real and fake pairs as training data: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11835 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17671. Own round 1: within-host paired head with a variance penalty (ideas/IDEAS_v1.md, M3) and the mirror self-morph as a negative (D2). Already registered in-house: twins plus history crossing with two-person morphs (SM1 arm e). What remains new: the mirror image as blending partner (not found in one search; absence not proven), exact twins crossed with history as negatives of self-made positives, and a controlled comparison with SelfMAD on the same 25,000 renders. The loss is not new. A within-host dose-ranking loss in morph detection was not found (one search, not verified).
cards.strongest_objection: It rebuilds SelfMAD, the release that fails hardest in our audit, and the two fixes it relies on are not shown to work. Measured but unreviewed: the one-person head beats one band-power statistic by 0.021 [-0.037, 0.081], below the 0.05 mark the paired-differences experiment (PD1) registered itself (experiments/PD1_signal-isolation-paired-differences/landmark/first_pass_dino_opencv_fold0.json). The ablation meant to tie audit and method may show nothing: a plain head on frozen CLIP at 224 px flags only 3 to 6% of history-matched FRLL genuine photos (experiments/AF0/cn0.json, unreviewed), and the history failure is established for SelfMAD and MADation ViT-B/16, not for the ViT-L/14 recipe the idea uses. The claim 'the same thing at growing dose' is contradicted: the mirror step is the most separable (0.98 to 0.99) at the lowest dose (9.6 against 15.1 and 18.8 grey levels) and the one-person head scores mirror blends like two-person morphs (0.486). The claim that no loss term lets a file or source property in is wrong as stated: all genuine images at one constant and every blend a margin above its twin compares them anyway; protection comes from what is in the pool, and a normal two-class loss on the same pool has it too.
cards.likeliest_confound: Softness is the cheapest: a blend has about half the Laplacian variance of its halves and one statistic reaches 0.912 where the head reaches 0.933. The proposed crossed contrast is one-sided because softened copies exist only for zero-dose images; control: a full 2 x 2 of {native, softened} x {twin, blend} on the same 200 hosts, which needs 1,200 softened blends built with the verified shrink-and-enlarge call. Second: left-right symmetry. A mirror blend at fraction a has its asymmetry cut by (1 - 2a) against its twin in every variant, a perfect within-host dose proxy with no doubled structure; a training-free mirror distance already isolates mirror blends at AUC 1.0 (experiments/AF0/mirror_clip224.json). Control: heads trained on mirror pairs only and on same-person pairs only, read against the mirror distance among untouched photos and on mirror blend against two-person morph. Third: only the registered history strengths are seen (one strength for SMDD renders); control: leave one strength out. Fourth, SMDD-only variant: every training image is a StyleGAN2 render; control: threshold from a camera-photo development pool.
cards.revised_design: Run it as arms of the registered SMDD rebuild (SM1), not as a second pipeline: the MADation recipe (CLIP ViT-L/14, LoRA, linear header) and its normal two-class loss stay unchanged and only the training images change. Arms at equal counts: (N) one-person blends against plain renders; (TW) blends against their exact warp-only twins plus plain renders; (TX) TW with every image also at the registered shrink strength; (TX2) TX with two-person morphs, which is SM1 arm (e) and the reference. The pair term plus noise term is one optional arm, kept only if it lowers the flag rate of an unseen genuine source at the development threshold. Partner: the same person's second photo where it exists (FRGC, colorFERET); the mirror partner only if it passes the symmetry test; otherwise the SMDD-only variant needs a shifted-copy partner through the approved warp path (lead's yes, verification against the unchanged tool), stated openly as SelfMAD's construction with twins. A symmetric decoy enters as a zero-dose image only with a yes and only if the mirror partner is used. One registered history strength is left out of training and tested. If arm N on ViT-L/14 flags at most 10% of history-matched genuine photos, the claim 'twins and crossing remove the failure' is void for this recipe; the same four image sets are then fitted on the SelfMAD backbone (HRNet-W18, own crop) or the claim is dropped. The threshold comes from a camera-photo development pool, never from renders or FRLL. The claim is 'two face images were mixed'; mirror and same-person blends go into the single-subject table, pending the author's ruling. Test time: one image, one forward pass, one fixed threshold, no twin, no gate.
cards.first_test: Frozen features, linear heads, half a day. cards.name: Noise-only mirror mix: one-photo positives for diffusion morphs
cards.one_line: Keep it as a small audit of which input makes a diffusion morph look like a morph (fresh-noise render and single-code mixes scored by existing heads); the training use is dropped for this deadline.
cards.novelty: Diffusion autoencoders (CVPR 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.15640) already report what the write-up lists as unmeasured: with the semantic code fixed, changing the noise map 'only affects minor details, such as the hair and skin details, the eyes, or the mouth', and encoded maps 'show some residual details and do not look normally distributed' (quotes as returned by a page-reading tool on the ar5iv copy; PDF not read by me). Inverted noise maps are not white noise: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03027 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06140 (search summaries). MorDIFF (https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01843) mixes both codes; no one-code ablation found. DiM (https://arxiv.org/html/2301.04218v4): variants change only the noise path (A: lerp of semantic code and slerp of noise; B: lerp of noise; C, their default: a pixel-averaged pre-morph is given to the stochastic encoder; D: an OpenCV morph as pre-morph); none mixes one code only and none asks what a detector reads (from the tool's reading of the HTML). What remains new: single-code mixes and a fresh-noise render used to attribute a detector's response, and a one-photo positive for diffusion morphs. Not found in two searches; absence not proven.
cards.strongest_objection: It cannot be built in time as a method and nothing shows it is needed. No image of the design exists: the 32-person codes are not written (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AD1b/gen is absent; the run was at 32 of 80 inversions after 5,108 s), the 536-host set has not started because Athena takes no jobs, and one inversion costs about 160 s on the DGX. The diffusion first pass (unreviewed) already shows that a head trained on same-person mixes of two real photos transfers to two-person morphs at 0.955, so a one-photo positive is needed only to scale to one-photo sources, which is the 40 GPU-hour part. The state-of-the-art path names a column that is in no published table: on morph against camera photo the same head reaches 0.876 where PNG size alone gives 0.877, and reconstructions score below photos (0.26). In DiM variant C the noise map comes from a pixel-averaged pre-morph, so the trace a noise-only mix teaches may not be the trace in those cells.
cards.likeliest_confound: Cheapest: 'the noise map is not this photo's own inversion'. A reconstruction uses the exact inverted map of its photo; a mixed map or fresh random noise both break that fit, so a head can read the misfit and not mixing. Control: the fresh-noise render, measured first, because it also bears on every existing 'morph against reconstruction' number. Second: symmetry of the fine-detail layer. If the encoder is close to flip-equivariant, the spherical mix of a noise map with its mirror's map is a left-right symmetric map, so 'no symmetric face' holds for layout only (not measured). Control: on saved codes, the cosine between the noise map of the flipped photo and the flipped noise map; replace the mirror by another person's noise map with the host's semantic code. Third: detail energy changes when two nearly orthogonal maps are mixed; control: simple-statistic floor per arm at the input size and on the centre crop, equal step count.
cards.revised_design: Use it as an audit of the two codes, not as a training method for this deadline. Arms per host with the unchanged encoder, mixing and render functions at 20 steps and one writer: reconstruction; fresh-noise render (host semantic code, new random noise, two draws); noise-only mix with another person's noise map; semantic-only mix with another person; the full published mix; noise-only mirror mix kept only as a symmetry probe. First score the arms with heads that already exist (the one-person and two-person heads of the diffusion arm of PD1, fitted on 516 FRGC and colorFERET hosts); FRLL persons are scored only. If the fresh-noise render is flagged, every 'morph against reconstruction' number in the paper is printed beside 'morph against fresh-noise render'. A face-recognition check per arm decides whether the noise-only mix with another person is a one-identity image. Partners are neutral photos only. The 536-host version (DG1 set B) and any training use wait for a clear first result and an open cluster. Calling the unchanged functions with one code swapped adds no image operation but needs the lead's yes.
cards.first_test: Step 0, CPU, minutes, file that exists: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AD1b/smoke_gen/codes_xT.npz (4 persons; later /mnt/t7/smad_next/AD1b/gen/codes_xT.npz with 32 persons, not yet written): cosine between the noise map of the flipped photo and the flipped noise map of the photo; lag-1 autocorrelation of a map and its correlation with the photo's Laplacian. Step 1, small GPU job, needs the lead's yes: for the persons with saved codes (32 with photo and mirror, 16 with a second photo and another person) render the six arms at 20 steps, about 200 renders, 5 minutes to 1 hour of the shared GPU. Step 2, CPU: CLIP ViT-L/14 pooled features as in PD1 (training features exist in /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/diffae/feat/clip/), scored with the existing PD1 one-person and two-person heads. Metric: share of persons whose arm scores above their own reconstruction, exact binomial interval, with the seven simple statistics of FZ1 beside it. Decisive version only after that: the same arms for the 536 hosts of DG1 set B (inputs aligned in /mnt/t7/smad_next/DG1/pool_a256; nothing generated yet).
cards.pass_and_kill: Only clear outcomes count with 16 to 32 persons. Kill of the training idea: the fresh-noise render scores above the reconstruction in 90% or more of persons under both heads; then heads read the misfit to the photo's own inversion, the audit finding stays and the twin changes. Kill of the noise arm: noise-only mix at 60% or less while the semantic-only mix is at 90% or more. Pass to the 536-host run: fresh-noise at 60% or less and noise-only mix at 90% or more; decisive bar there: a head trained on noise-only mixes against reconstructions and fresh-noise renders reaches at least 0.85 on full two-person morphs, within 0.05 of the two-person head and 0.05 above the statistic floor. Mirror partner dropped for the noise arm if the step-0 cosine is 0.5 or more. Anything between the bars: no decision before the 536-host set exists.
cards.compute: Step 0: CPU minutes. Step 1: at most 1 shared-GPU hour (1 s per 20-step render when idle; far slower under load). Step 2: CPU minutes. Decisive part: about 3,200 extra 20-step renders on top of the inversions already planned in DG1, about 1 GPU-hour at the idle rate; A100 rate not measured; needs Athena. Training use at 5,000 hosts (about 40 GPU-hours at the idle-DGX rate): not in this sprint.
cards.reason: The fresh-noise twin may change how the established diffusion contrast and the frozen-feature probes are read, which matters for the audit, and no prior work was found that attributes a detector's response to one of the two codes. As a method its positive carries two cheap cues, it has no path to the published columns, and it has no data before the cluster opens.

cards.name: Dose-matched test and optional head for the second-identity step
cards.one_line: Keep a reporting control that reads probe score against measured in-face disagreement for same-person and two-person blends, gated by a face-recognition validity check; no identity head is trained.
cards.novelty: Ferrara, Franco and Maltoni, 'Decoupling texture blending and shape warping in face morphing', BIOSIG 2019 (https://dl.gi.de/handle/20.500.12116/34232): separate factors for shape and texture, studied for attack success (bibliographic record only, content not read). Selfmorphs as genuine or as attack: MorDeephy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03110), MorphGuard (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10497) and the sources in 14_CLASS_DEFINITIONS.md; none compares a same-person and a two-person blend at equal blend strength. What remains new: the dose-matched contrast itself (not found in one targeted search; not proven absent). It is a control, small in scope.
cards.strongest_objection: One matched scalar does not isolate identity, and the matched morph may stop being an attack. Matching mean disagreement leaves free where the disagreement sits, the mixing fraction (hence warp distance) and averaged shape (0.687 on exact shapes), so a pass may read any of these and a fail on 300 hosts with mean-pooled frozen features may lack power. The whole-frame dose (15.1 against 18.8 grey levels) includes clothing and background of two sessions; inside the face a same-person blend may disagree far less, the matched two-person fraction may fall to 0.2 or lower, and such a blend may no longer verify against the partner, which makes it no morphing attack by the definitions. The expectation 'small' does not fit the unmatched numbers (0.88 to 0.93 on detector features, experiments/AR1/README.md; 0.82 to 0.83 as a CLIP projection, unreviewed). Record errors: features of the graded set are not cached yet (no file at 18:14); the FaceMorpher warp-only image is the exact twin of the same-person blend only, so the proposed dose proxy is biased; the head 'rides on Idea 1's fits', which may not happen.
cards.likeliest_confound: Cheapest: residual dose. Graded levels are 0.1 apart and the proxy 'pixel difference to the warp-only image' includes warp displacement on the two-person side only. Control: measure dose as the disagreement of the two warped images inside the face at build time (the AF0 path does this), print that statistic's own AUC on the matched pairs and require it near 0.5. Then softness (27 statistics on the matched pairs, excess over the best), shape averaging (exact landmark-shape score printed beside the probe), ghosted clothing and background of two sessions (constant-colour blanking outside the face), and the FaceMorpher surround (OpenCV-style engine decides).
cards.revised_design: Reporting control only; no second output is trained. With the OpenCV-style engine through the verified AF0 path, build for the 536 ladder hosts the same-person blend at 0.5 and two-person blends at 0.1 to 0.5, each in its own mean shape, and record the measured disagreement of the two warped images inside the face at build time. Blank everything outside the face with one constant colour. Validity gate first: only two-person levels where at least 70% of blends verify against both contributors count as attacks. Read a curve of probe score against measured disagreement for both partner types; the deciding number is the within-host contrast at the valid two-person level closest in disagreement to the host's same-person blend. Probe: logistic head on CLIP and DINOv3 mean features, 5 folds by person, with a power check on the unmatched contrast. Beside it: the dose statistic's own AUC on the matched pairs, the best of the 27 simple statistics, and the exact landmark-shape score. A host-shape (texture-only) version is added only if the changed target shape is verified against the unchanged tool. The result fixes the paper's wording and the reading of the single-subject table.
cards.first_test: Existing images, to decide whether the build is worth it: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/fm_graded/m000..m050 (300 hosts, 300 files per level, checked) and /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/facemorpher/R3 (536, checked). CPU: mean absolute pixel difference to the host's m000 image inside the landmark hull for the graded levels and for the same-person blend (one reference for both sides), the level at which the doses cross, simple statistics from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/. Features of the graded set are missing and queued (list /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/lists/ar1g.csv). FaceMorpher is descriptive. Deciding version: the build above (about 3,200 new images of an approved kind), CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 ViT-L/16 mean features, face-recognition embeddings for the graded levels, logistic head with 5 folds by person, metric = within-host matched AUC with person bootstrap. About 2 CPU hours for the existing-image part, half a day for the deciding version.
cards.pass_and_kill: Void: at the dose-matched level fewer than 70% of two-person blends verify against both contributors; reported as a finding (at equal in-face disagreement a two-person blend is no longer an attack, so dose and second identity cannot be separated on landmark morphs). Kill (no identity claim): matched AUC below 0.60 with upper bound below 0.65 on both feature sets while the same recipe reaches 0.85 or more on the unmatched contrast. Pass (identity-specific trace readable): matched AUC at least 0.75, lower bound above 0.65, at least 0.05 above the largest of the dose statistic, the 27 simple statistics and the shape score. Between: reported as open and the wording stays 'mixing'.
cards.compute: Existing-image part: CPU only, about 2 hours, plus features of 1,800 graded images that are already queued. Deciding version: under an hour of CPU builds when the machine is idle (longer under load), 0.3 to 0.5 shared-GPU hours of features, face-recognition embeddings on the GPU (that route hit out-of-memory errors today). No training run.
cards.reason: It is cheap and protects the central wording of the paper, and the validity gate can turn a void result into a finding. It moves no benchmark number and its answer depends on how dose is defined.

vetting.cross_cutting: The mirror partner carries a measured by-product in every family: on the landmark ladder the mirror step is the most separable (0.98 to 0.99, unreviewed) at the lowest dose and a training-free symmetry score isolates mirror blends at 1.0; in the diffusion autoencoder the mirror mix has asymmetry 2.1 against 18.3 (4 persons), and the mirror rungs planned at fraction 0.5 in the diffusion and MIPGAN generation jobs (DG1, AG1) inherit this. The softness control is one-sided today: softened copies exist only for zero-dose images, so no head can yet be shown to read blending and not sharpness. The history failure is established for SelfMAD and MADation ViT-B/16, while a plain frozen CLIP head at 224 px does not show it (experiments/AF0/cn0.json, unreviewed), so the chain 'failure, then a protocol that removes it' still needs the failure shown on the ViT-L/14 recipe or an HRNet arm. The exact reconstruction may be too easy a twin for diffusion morphs; a fresh-noise render belongs beside it before more weight is put on 'morph against reconstruction' numbers. The honest diffusion column is not a published column: on morph against camera photo the paired heads do not beat PNG size (0.876 against 0.877, unreviewed), so the state-of-the-art claim on diffusion cells cannot come from this lens. Pair statistics overstate one-image performance; print the unpaired number beside every paired one and compare any new loss with an ordinary unpaired head. The rulings on same-person blends disagree (morph; side study; third category) and Idea 1 trains them as positives, so the author's yes or no is needed before tables are laid out. Athena does not accept jobs yet and notebook entries carry times later than the machine clock, so only frozen-feature tests are safe before 14 Nov.

vetting.lens: What frozen foundation features read, and a shared mixing direction (hostile review by a CVPR area chair with an image-forensics and morph-detection background)

cards.name: Three-level ordinal score trained on trace-matched one-person twins
cards.one_line: On the landmark family only, train the MADation recipe three ways on identical history-crossed images (same-person twins as genuine, twins as attack, three ordered levels) and keep the ordinal label only if its two-person-over-twin reading survives a warp-size control at equal benchmark error.
cards.novelty: Found: the two endpoints are published labelling habits. Same-person selfmorphs as genuine: MorDeephy (ICPRAM 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03110). Self-blended one-image attacks: SelfMAD (FG 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05504). Reading two identities from one image: OrthoMAD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07841) and IDistill (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03002). Ordinal losses are standard (CORAL, CORN; survey https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00952). A three-class scheme exists only for differential detection (Bologna group; seen in a search result, paper not opened). Round 1 already had mixing-fraction regression (T6) and shrink-factor regression (M5). Not found: a three-level ordered label for single-image detection, or a three-arm comparison of the two habits. Not verified by me: MorphGuard (arXiv 2505.10497), Kashiani IJCB 2023, Borghi 2021 (taken from 14_CLASS_DEFINITIONS.md). Web search stopped after 14 searches (session budget), so absence claims are weak.
cards.strongest_objection: The upper level is not shown to be a second-person reading, and the first test is nearly decided before it runs. Measured (unreviewed): a direct probe already separates same-person from two-person landmark morphs at 0.88 to 0.93 (experiments/AR1/README.md, gate G-c) and a CLIP mean-difference direction gives 0.82 (PD1 landmark q1_clip_mean.json), so the 0.80 pass mark is met by default. The mirror pass mark is void: a 32-pixel thumbnail separates mirror self-morph from two-person morph at 0.93 and the background alone at 0.90 (experiments/AR1/baselines.json). SMDD has one render per identity, so its only twin is the mirror twin. On diffusion the wanted order is violated: same-person mixes score above two-person morphs (0.25 and 0.44) and photos above reconstructions (0.26) (PD1 diffusion first pass, one fold). On GAN the upper level tops at 0.61 to 0.66. Putting reconstructions at level 1 while SMDD StyleGAN2 renders sit at level 0 trains a generator-fingerprint split. No table number rises, and the 'threshold choice' hides that at the upper threshold only a 0.65 to 0.85 margin is left.
cards.likeliest_confound: Warp size and source disparity. The two-person warp moves the host further and ghosts hair, collar and glasses more; the record notes a same-person morph already shows a ghosted background and clothing outline. File-size softness is excluded (PNG size 0.51 for same-person vs two-person), warp size is not. Our partners are look-alikes (median FR cosine 0.234 against 0.04 to 0.12 in benchmarks), so the reading is also untested at benchmark similarity. Controls: (1) print the simple-statistic floor for same-person vs two-person from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/ar1.npz; (2) AUC inside the overlap band of landmark shape distance, and partial correlation of the score with FR dissimilarity given shape distance; (3) a new warp-only rung toward the mean shape of host and other person (approved warp path, CPU minutes; round-1 idea D4), which the upper-level read-out must not separate from the existing warp-only rung; (4) mirror twins are evaluation-only.
cards.revised_design: Scope is the landmark family; generator families are report-only. Three arms on the MADation recipe (CLIP ViT-L/14 with LoRA, one linear head) use identical images and identical softening: (A) same-person twins labelled genuine, (B) twins labelled attack, (C) three ordered levels. Level 0 holds camera photos, their E7 (shrink-and-enlarge) copies and warp-only images of both warp sizes; level 1 holds same-person two-session morphs only; level 2 holds two-person morphs; softened copies keep their level. Mirror self-morphs, generator reconstructions and generator mixes get no label and are only scored; SMDD renders stay genuine as in the published protocol. The ordinal form is chosen on frozen features: a shared-direction cumulative link if the trace direction and the second-identity direction have cosine at least 0.5, otherwise a two-step head (manipulated, then two persons given manipulated), which needs the author's ruling that two logits of one network combined by a fixed rule are not score fusion. There is no tie penalty in the main arms (an earlier consistency loss gave no gain, A49, not re-verified); it is one optional ablation. A fixed person-disjoint set of 107 hosts is held out before any fit. Reported for every arm and every released detector: benchmark error with the neutral-only genuine column, E7 flag rate at the 5% threshold, two-person vs same-person AUC with its floor and inside the shape-distance overlap band, the share of two-person morphs caught at the threshold that flags 5% of same-person twins, and where warp-only, mirror and reconstruction images land. All seeds are reported.
cards.first_test: Frozen features, CPU, 2 to 3 hours. Data (all listed and present): pooled CLIP features /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat/clip224/ar1.npz (mean patch token, class token); DINOv3 mean patch token from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/dinov3_512/ar1.tokens.npy; genuine photos native and E7 from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/clip224/bench_s.tokens.npy; simple statistics /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/ar1.npz; landmark files and FR embeddings under /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/; zero-field images of the alpha-field probe (/mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat/clip224/af0.npz) as a descriptive warp control. Heads, linear, five person folds of the paired-differences landmark run: (A) two-person vs {photo, warp-only, same-person}; (B) {same-person, two-person} vs {photo, warp-only}; (C1) cumulative link; (C2) two-step. Metrics on held-out hosts, OpenCV-style engine decides: M1 two-person vs same-person AUC and excess over the floor; M2 the same inside the shape-distance overlap band, plus two-person-shape warp vs same-person-shape warp under the upper-level read-out; M3 two-person vs {photo, warp-only}; M4 E7 flag rate on FRLL and MAD22 genuine photos at the 5% threshold; M5 share of two-person morphs caught at the threshold flagging 5% of same-person twins; M6 cosine between trace and second-identity directions; M7 fit on one engine, score the other. The clean warp rung adds CPU minutes and about ten GPU-minutes of features.
cards.pass_and_kill: Pass (ordinal earns GPU time): arm C within 0.01 of the better binary arm on M3, within 0.03 of arm A on M1, M4 at most 10%, and M2 holds (AUC in the overlap band at least 0.65 with lower bound above 0.55; the two warp sizes at most 0.60). Kill 1 (label adds nothing): arm A matches arm B on M3 within 0.01 and on M4 within 3 points; then 'twins as genuine' is used, the three-arm table is reported as a finding and no ordinal network is trained. I expect Kill 1 (one-fold record: two-person head 0.980 vs one-person head 0.933 on warp-only vs two-person, 0.759 vs 0.652 on same-person vs two-person). Kill 2 (upper level reads warp size): M2 below 0.60 in the overlap band or the two warp sizes at 0.65 or more; the column is renamed 'source disparity' and no second-person claim is made. Kill 3: M4 above 15% for arm C while a binary arm is at 10% or less.
cards.compute: First test: 0 GPU-hours (about ten GPU-minutes if the clean warp rung is built), 2 to 3 CPU-hours. Full, only after a pass: three arms, three seeds, about 3 A100-hours per fit (generator's estimate, not measured on Athena), about 27 A100-hours. Needs the SMDD rebuild (re-staging) and Athena (no job accepted at 17:40).
cards.reason: It raises no table number and its second-person column is confounded with warp size until the missing rung is built, but a three-arm labelling comparison is a clean, modestly new result on a documented split in the literature. The frozen-feature test is feasible today; the trained version is tight in three days and limited to 536 twin hosts.

cards.name: Code-factorised one-person twins for diffusion and GAN morphs
cards.one_line: Use the unchanged diffusion autoencoder to render one-person control cells (noise code mixed with fresh Gaussian noise, with the mirror, with another person; semantic-only mix) as an audit instrument that says what the probe and the one separating release read, with no training use before 14 Nov.
cards.novelty: Found: the two-part code is the published design of the diffusion autoencoder (Preechakul et al., CVPR 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.15640, abstract read). Fast-DiM (Blasingame and Liu, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09484, page fetched) states the morph rule (average of semantic codes, slerp of noise codes at 0.5) and has one partial ablation: white noise in place of the encoded noise code with the averaged semantic code, measured for attack strength, not detection; it reports no noise-only or semantic-only mix. MorDIFF (https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01843) interpolates both codes with no one-person control. Matched reconstructions as hard negatives exist in generated-image detection: DRCT (ICML 2024, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/chen24ay.html), Aligned Datasets (ICLR 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11835). Not found: partial-code mixes as one-person controls or training negatives in morph detection. My search budget ended before a dedicated query, so 'not found' is weak.
cards.strongest_objection: The registered first test is already answered, and the design cannot tell 'two noise codes were mixed' from 'detail was regenerated'. Measured (unreviewed, one fold, FERET and FRGC pool): the head trained on two-person morphs scores same-person mixes against reconstructions at 0.991, which is the pass branch of the cross-application test. Under the mix-trained head camera photos score above reconstructions (0.26), and diffusion morphs are sharper than reconstructions (Laplacian variance 0.966 at 100 steps), so the direction points from a smooth 20-step reconstruction toward a photo. A noise mix with another person's code does not separate the two readings. On the published contrast (morph vs camera photo) the mix-trained head equals PNG size (0.876 vs 0.877), so there is no route to the published MorDIFF cell. The adapted releases already fail morph vs reconstruction (0.40 to 0.49), so the new cell adds a figure, not a finding, for them.

cards.name: Ladder-selected layers and tokens with a fixed nuisance eraser
cards.one_line: Dropped as a method; its final-block read-out comparison moves into the first test of idea 1 and its projection is already question Q4 of the paired-differences experiment (PD1).
cards.novelty: Found: closed-form linear erasure is LEACE (NeurIPS 2023, https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/d066d21c619d0a78c5b557fa3291a8f4-Abstract.html), with a guarantee against linear readers only. Intermediate CLIP blocks with learned block weights for forensic detection: RINE (ECCV 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19091). Freezing a principal subspace and adapting the rest: Effort (ICML 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15633). In morph detection: MADation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03800); R-FLoRA (arXiv 2604.17321) seen in one search snippet only, not opened. Inside our programme the same eraser on pooled features is round-1 idea M3 (ideas/IDEAS_v1.md) and question Q4 of the paired-differences experiment. What remains new is choosing the junction block by ladder selectivity, which is a tuning rule.
cards.strongest_objection: It contradicts an established fact and, where measured, has nothing to erase. Frozen features already carry storage history: the frozen-encoder ViT-B/16 release moves from 39.7% to 69.6% flagged, and a genuine-only statistic fails the history control in CLIP (0.582), DINOv3 (0.356) and diffusion-autoencoder features (0.000) (ID0 result.md, unreviewed). A linear eraser at one block does not bind trainable blocks above it; they can rebuild softness from second-order token statistics, which the write-up itself lists as a read-out. On the GAN family, removing the softening direction changed the AUC by 0.001 and the flag rate from 4.4% to 3.9% (PD1 gan res_clip_pool.json, Q4, unreviewed), because twin-paired heads already sat at 4 to 8%. It re-proposes a round-1 idea, which the brief forbids unchanged, and its 24-block profile plus 10 to 20 fits competes with the main chain for the same three days.

About 290 block, token and read-out cells are tested against three thresholds on 107 held-out hosts, so one 'selective' cell is likely by chance; control: select on four folds of the OpenCV-style engine, confirm on the fifth fold and on FaceMorpher. A low E7 flag rate after erasure is explained most cheaply by the eraser having seen the same two E7 strengths; control: fit the softening direction on the 80-pixel SMDD copies only and test on FRLL and MAD22 photos. An expression direction fitted on FRLL pairs would be fitted on benchmark genuine photos that also differ in capture detail (1.43 times file size).

cards.name: Layer-count evidence: two superposed textures against one softened texture
cards.one_line: Keep the bracketing test (a morph must outrank a sharper AND a softer negative of the same host) as an evaluation instrument for every detector; give the fourth-order layer-count statistic one CPU test judged by what it adds to the 26 registered energy statistics; make the layer-count map a training target only if that test passes.
cards.novelty: Found by search (9 searches ran, then the shared search budget was used up). The layer law is the central-limit argument of independent component analysis, used to separate two superimposed images: Farid and Adelson, JOSA A 1999 (https://persci.mit.edu/pub_abstracts/farid_josa_99_abs.html; abstract page read). Fourth-order wavelet statistics are old forensic features: Farid and Lyu, CVPR Workshops 2003 (https://mlanthology.org/cvprw/2003/farid2003cvprw-higherorder); Lyu and Farid, IEEE TSP 2005 (https://cse.buffalo.edu/~siweilyu/papers/sp05.pdf); abstracts only. Band-pass kurtosis is a noise meter: Zoran and Weiss, ICCV 2009 (https://people.csail.mit.edu/danielzoran/zoranweiss09.pdf). The proposed ratio mean|c| / rms(c) is the normalised sparsity measure of Krishnan, Tay and Fergus, CVPR 2011 (https://mlanthology.org/cvpr/2011/krishnan2011cvpr-blind), introduced because blur raises it (direction read in a secondary source only): this contradicts the claimed blur invariance. Morph detection neighbours: PRNU variance across image cells, Debiasi et al., BTAS 2018 (https://christoph-busch.de/files/Debiasi-PRNU-variance-MAD-BTAS-2018.pdf; first three pages read); a morph decomposed into two faces from one image, Banerjee, Jaiswal and Ross, IJCB 2022 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.02933) and Shukla and Ross, IJCB 2024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.10993); search results only, papers not opened. NOT found in one search: a morph detection paper with a layer-count target or a two-sided (sharper and softer) negative test; the second, targeted search could not run. NOT verified: the generator's citations Levin and Weiss, and Pan, Zhang and Lyu. What remains new: the bracketing test as a stated protocol in morph detection and a contrast-free dense target; the statistic is textbook.
cards.strongest_objection: The statistic is not blind to blur and the law can act in about one octave. A blur is a sum of neighbouring samples of one layer and lowers sparsity by the same mechanism as a second layer (the l1/l2 ratio is a published blur measure). The responses the registered statistics already compute (Laplacian, one-level Haar, 3x3 noise residual; cue_floor.py lines 74 to 108) live in the top octave, which the registered 61.2 px history empties (cut-off about 0.23 cycles/pixel at IED 130; my arithmetic). One sanity photo in /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AS0_mirror-asymmetry/check.json has odd-to-even energy 0.82 at 4 to 8 px wavelength, 0.52 at 8 to 16 px and 0.17 at 16 to 32 px, so two aligned faces are unrelated layers only from about 0.125 cycles/pixel upward: the band 0.125 to 0.25 is the only one where the law acts and content survives, and the stronger history reshapes it (expected, not measured). Pooled face-box kurtosis is dominated by the shared variance mixture of anatomy, which averaging does not change. The training target inherits round 2's objections: t is largest where both energies are small and equal (flat skin) unless a free noise floor zeroes it, and a map that is zero on every negative still fits 'global flag times anatomy template' (first dense pass: map quality 0.275 against template 0.231, /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AF0/README.md section 5, unreviewed). The dose-shape audit of released detectors is not identified, because any monotone squashing of a score changes the share reached at a = 0.25.
cards.likeliest_confound: Spectral shape read by two or three registered band powers: averaging lowers all bands above the alignment scale by a flat factor (measured 0.52 for the Laplacian), shrink-and-enlarge removes everything above one cut-off, so a logistic head on band powers can rank a morph above both a sharper and a softened negative without counting layers; the bracket excludes a function of ONE sharpness number, not of two. Control: the 26 registered statistics through the same head and the same bracket (energy-only head); the fourth-order numbers count only by what they add (paired difference with interval). Second confound: noise and compression level of the photo pool (kurtosis reads noise; smiling FRLL files are larger and noisier). Controls: genuine FRGC against genuine colorFERET at most 0.60, FRLL neutral against smiling at most 0.60, R0 against softened R0 at both strengths inside 0.45 to 0.55. Limit to state: only one softening family (shrink-and-enlarge, two strengths) is allowed, so nothing is shown about defocus, denoising or JPEG.
cards.revised_design: Split the idea into three parts that stand or fall alone. (A) Bracketing test as an evaluation instrument for every detector, released ones and ours, within host on the OpenCV-style engine: two-person morph against its warp-only image (negative sharper); two-person morph against the warp-only image softened at 61.2 px (negative softer, checked per pair by face-box Laplacian variance); softened morph against unsoftened warp-only image; the 112.7 px copy is reported as the sharpness-matched negative. The one number is the weakest leg, printed beside the same number for the energy-only head. Part A needs 400 new files: the 200 ladder two-person morphs through the approved, unchanged shrink-and-enlarge path at both strengths. (B) Layer-count statistic as a measurement: kurtosis and l1/l2 ratio per 32-px block of the face box, median over blocks, in the bands 0.0625 to 0.125 and 0.125 to 0.25 cycles/pixel (in-memory band images, as the mirror-asymmetry test AS0 already registers), plus the registered Laplacian, Haar and noise-residual responses for reference. B is judged by what it adds to the 26 registered statistics. (C) Only if B passes: the layer map becomes a sixth arm of the registered five-arm ablation, noise floor fixed beforehand, with the registered target check (flat below busy, contrast correlation below 0.3); test time stays one forward pass, mean of the top tenth of patch predictions in the face box. The dose shape is reported for the statistic only. Same-person morphs and mirror self-blends will be flagged and go to the single-subject table. Diffusion and GAN reads are secondary and descriptive.

cards.name: Left-right parity ratio: asymmetry shrinks when two faces average
cards.one_line: Reduce to one evidence row (odd-to-even energy ratio in the coarse bands, no training) measured inside the already running mirror-asymmetry test (AS0), with a pool-offset control added; drop the two-view trained form and the 'same signal for every generator' claim until AS0 reports.
cards.novelty: Found by search: deepfake detection uses symmetry in the opposite direction (generated faces break it): Li, Cao and Zhao, 'Exploiting facial symmetry to expose deepfakes', ICIP 2021, pages 3587 to 3591 (https://dblp.org/rec/conf/icip/LiCZ21; listing and search summary read, paper not opened); a later 'Forensic symmetry for deepfakes' (IEEE TIFS 2023) appeared in results, could not be opened, authors not verified. Morph detection: one search found no paper using left-right image symmetry; the landmark-geometry paper it returned (Autherith and Pasquini, J. Imaging 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8321196/, opened) is differential and has no symmetry feature; a 2026 preprint (Ivanovska and Struc, https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15461) was returned with a snippet about symmetry in language-model explanations, which its abstract does not mention. A second search could not run (search budget used up), so 'not used in morph detection' rests on one search. NOT verified: the psychology references (averaged faces are more symmetric). Inside our record the raw idea is M1 of round 1 and the registered experiment AS0 (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AS0_mirror-asymmetry/prereg.md), which already fixes the band ratio, symmetric mask, shape asymmetry, covariates, history controls and pass and kill marks. New in the write-up: the photo-bound against person-bound split on genuine photos, the look-alike prediction, the two-view trained form.
cards.strongest_objection: The effect lives only in the coarse bands, where it is small against pose and lighting, and it reads 'two captures were averaged', not 'two persons'. The ratio can fall only where even parts of two faces are related and odd parts are not; in texture bands both halve and the ratio stays (one sanity photo in AS0's check.json: ratio 0.97, 0.82, 0.52 below 16 px wavelength, 0.17 and lower above; the morph keeps 0.52 of the Laplacian variance). A 2 to 3 dB fall against a spread of several dB gives 0.6 to 0.7, which is what the raw reads show: 0.675 and 0.571 folded for photo against two-person morph, 0.662 and 0.589 for warp-only against two-person morph, and only 0.608 and 0.553 for same-person against two-person morph (/home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AF0/mirror_clip224.json, preliminary, unreviewed). A morph-free score of low odd energy calls a strictly frontal, evenly lit, neutral photo a morph and its threshold moves with the photo pool; the closed form of the same kind overshot every image-feature arm of the identity-shrinkage triage (ID0) by 0.24 to 0.51 AUC. The exact invariance is algebra for pixel band energies only: in CLIP tokens the native against history-matched read is off 0.5 in 5 of 7 cells (0.464 to 0.491, intervals exclude 0.5), so 'evidence that provably cannot come from a symmetric cue' is false in feature space, where softness shrinks the odd part. The two-view form keeps every shortcut in its even branch, is close to a fusion of two scores, and costs 25 A100-hours. The write-up's kill (below 0.65) can hardly fire, since the untrained read is already 0.662.
cards.likeliest_confound: Capture conditions: yaw, lighting direction, hair and expression set the coarse-band odd energy and differ by photo pool and by expression (the genuine class of 12 of 17 cells is half smiling; FRLL contributors share one studio rig, so the lighting part does not halve there). Controls: negative class is the warp-only image or the same-person morph of the same host, never a camera photo of another pool; genuine against genuine across pools (R0 FRGC against R0 colorFERET; FRLL neutral against smiling of one person) at most 0.60; AS0's registered partial-out of yaw, lighting and Laplacian variance and its session strata; neutral photos only on FRLL cells. Frame content (one-sided watermark on corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher, mirror reads 0.94 and reversed 0.73): mirror-symmetric face mask only.
