cards.compute: 0 GPU-hours. AS0 is already running on CPU (2 processes); the three added reads need about one hour of CPU. The token read, only after a pass: about 1 CPU-hour on cached tokens. The dropped two-view form would have cost about 25 A100-hours.
cards.reason: It is nearly free because the registered mirror-asymmetry test already measures it, and its history control is the cleanest in the programme, but the expected read is 0.6 to 0.7, mostly not about identity, and confounded by pose, lighting and expression. Its morph-free form penalises the most compliant photos, so it can be an evidence row at most, not part of the network.

vetting.cross_cutting: The two ideas assume opposite things about the same bands: idea 1 needs the two faces to be unrelated layers in the mid bands, idea 2 needs their even parts to be strongly related there; the record (morph keeps 0.52 of the Laplacian variance; band power 0.125 to 0.25 cycles/pixel alone reaches 0.912, unreviewed) sides with 'unrelated' from about 8 px wavelength down, which leaves idea 1 one octave and idea 2 only the coarse bands. Everything measured today reads 'two captures were averaged', and neither idea changes that, so the paper should use those words and needs the author's ruling on the three-category class proposal. The bracketing test is the most useful piece of this lens: it is an evaluation protocol for every detector and costs 400 softened files, but first check whether a head on the 26 registered statistics passes it, because the bracket excludes one sharpness number, not spectral shape. 'Softness' here means one kernel family (shrink-and-enlarge at 112.7 and 61.2 px), so claims must be worded for that family; defocus, denoising and JPEG are untested. Softened copies of the AF0 halves did not exist at 18:28 (build running, training split only, strengths alternate per image) and softened ladder morphs do not exist, so within-pair softened tests must use the ladder copies or wait. The mirror-asymmetry test (AS0) already covers idea 2's pixel and shape tests with fixed pass and kill marks; no duplicate should start. The dose-shape reading is valid for a statistic in log units, not for a network score. Web search stopped after 9 searches when the shared session budget ran out, so the absence claims (no layer-count target, no bracketing test, no symmetry read in morph detection) rest on one search each and several references are marked unverified in the file.

vetting.lens: The single network that tops the published tables and passes the ladder (vetting by a hostile area chair)
vetting.cross_cutting: "Tops the published tables" cannot be claimed as written: published MAD22 values are on the original release while we score the corrected copy, the same release moves by 0.4 to 1.5 EER points between two machines (measured, experiments/RS1_own-crop-rescore/README.md 17:48), one genuine photo of 204 is 0.49 points, and the generator's own expected ranges straddle the published values on the two clean cells; the honest headline is the fixed-threshold miss rate among detectors that pass the controls. The ordered policy for one-photo generator output (policy O) trains the generator-fingerprint cue the paper attacks and conflicts with the author's position in 07_DECISIONS_NEEDED.md; policy A must be the headline. Today's unreviewed leads contradict the order the loss imposes (diffusion: same-person mixes score above two-person morphs, AUC 0.25; GAN mixing is latent averageness, 0.9998, with MIPGAN transfer 0.38 to 0.73; a mirror mix is a symmetric face, asymmetry 2.1 against 12 to 19.6), so the order term should be dropped. The first test of recipe 1 gates on the list bench_s, whose FRLL-Morphs rows are our aligned frames where the border alone gives 0.99 to 1.00; use corrected MAD22 OpenCV and Webmorph and the Poisson set (H1, measured bar 0.833) instead. The decisive softness control is crossed (genuine image softened to 61 px against a native morph of the same host) and needs no new image; of the registered strengths only 61.2 px on camera photos is useful (112.7 px is probably invisible at 224, the SMDD copy is about 20 px between the eyes), so SMDD alone cannot teach that softness is not blending. A frozen head cannot clear a LoRA network (the MADation-recipe ViT-L/14 retrains flag 59 to 87% of photos with the MorDIFF history, EV1 Part A.1), so every decisive first test needs real ViT-B/16 fits (0.87 h each on an A100, measured). Record disagreement to resolve: the "robust recipe" AMSL value of 15.0% EER (methods table row 13) against AUC 0.999 for the same networks in the fixed-threshold re-read (EV1 Part B.2). Literature search was cut short: ten searches and five abstracts, then the session's search budget ran out.

cards.name: Ladder-ordered training of one CLIP ViT-L/14 LoRA network
cards.one_line: Train one MADation-recipe CLIP ViT-L/14 LoRA network in which the morph's own warped halves, warp-only images and 61-pixel stored copies are genuine (policy A, no order term, an equality term only if the data protocol alone fails), and claim the best fixed-threshold miss rate among detectors that pass the storage and softness controls.
cards.novelty: Found: the equality term is the conditional variance penalty of Heinze-Deml and Meinshausen (Machine Learning 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.11469, abstract read) with host as the group. Inside morph detection: Kashiani et al., consistency regularization at logit and embedding level across morph-wise augmented views (IJCB 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10392, abstract read; augmentations not verified). Neighbouring field: CORE (Ni et al., CVPRW 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02749), QAD, one model tied across image qualities (Le and Woo, ICCV 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05911), DRCT, reconstructions as hard samples (ICML 2024, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/chen24ay.html). MorDeephy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03110) found; its same-person 'selfmorphs as genuine' detail is from our class page, not confirmed by my search. Our own note already holds BCE plus within-pair margin ranking on CLIP ViT-L with LoRA (03_LITERATURE_AND_METHODS.md, design M1). Backbone: MADation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03800). Remains new: the tied views (a morph's own warped halves, warp-only, storage crossed in both directions) and the fixed-threshold evaluation. Not found in ten searches: a morph-detection paper that ties warped halves to the genuine class. Search budget ran out; ranking losses in anti-spoofing not searched.
cards.strongest_objection: The route to the published level on the MAD22 mean and the generator cells runs through policy O, which is a trained generated-image detector and contradicts both the paper's audit and the author's position; without it the recipe reaches the published level on no more than the easy landmark cells, where differences are inside platform noise, so only a robustness claim remains, and nothing on disk shows that a LoRA fit (not a frozen head) passes the softness control.
cards.likeliest_confound: Softness: one band-power statistic separates warp-only from two-person morph at 0.912 against 0.980 for the head (unreviewed, PD1 landmark result), and the Laplacian floor is higher at 224 than at 512 (0.87 against 0.76, measured). Control: the crossed contrast (genuine image softened to 61 px against the native two-person morph of the same host; a softness reader falls below 0.5) plus every AUC printed as excess over the best statistic on the same images. Second: the aligner border if any cell is read on our frames (0.99 to 1.00); control: raw files through the face-detector crop, or only corrected MAD22 OpenCV and Webmorph and the Poisson set (H1). Third: symmetry and outline-ghost size planted by the order term; control: remove the order term.
cards.revised_design: One CLIP ViT-L/14 LoRA network, registered MADation recipe, last checkpoint, face-detector crop stored as PNG, loader resize to 224, no flip averaging; seed 401 is named now as the paper's network and seeds 402 to 405 give the spread. Policy A only: one-photo generator output is genuine; policy O is at most one labelled row. Genuine class: camera photos, SMDD renders, warp-only images, the morph's own warped halves and their 61.2 px stored copies; morph class: two-person morphs and their 61.2 px copies; the 112.7 px strength only if a statistic shows it is visible at 224; the 80 px SMDD copy is not a tied view. No order term; mirror and same-person rungs are never trained on and fill the single-subject table. Step 1 is data only with the unchanged training script; the equality term (squared logit difference between genuine views of one host) is written only if step 1 passes the signal marks and fails the shift mark. FRGC moves into training; a fixed seeded list of 200 landmark-ladder hosts is the test ladder and 100 more are the development ladder used for every go and no-go decision. Threshold: 5% false alarms on every development genuine pool with at least 60 px between the eyes. Diffusion rungs enter only after the SMDD-Ladder transfer test passes; GAN rungs do not enter. Reported: fixed-threshold miss per family with all history-matched pools protected (headline), native, history-matched and neutral-only EER on raw files, the crossed softness contrast, excess over the best statistic, the Poisson set, both class policies on generator cells, and released detectors through their own crop on the same files. Reference rows on the same data: MADation recipe on released SMDD, the same recipe on our data without halves and stored copies, history-only and label-permuted networks. Ablation table cut to eight rows at five seeds, with unseen-kernel pools (bicubic, Lanczos) in place of a left-out strength. Claim: best fixed-threshold miss among detectors that pass the controls; no state-of-the-art sentence for AMSL, GAN cells or MorDIFF.
cards.first_test: Tier 0 (tonight, CPU, no new image). Data, listed and present: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/feat/clip224/{af0_w1,af0_w2,af0_h,ar1,ar1soft,bench_s,h1}.tokens.npy, lists in /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/lists/, statistics in /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/{ar1,bench_s,h1,af0_w1}.npz (none yet for ar1soft: compute with the existing cues_all.py). Missing: the softened training list 'soft' (chain logged a failed try at 18:18; 1,819 of about 3,370 softened images exist) and softened ladder morphs. Features: mean-pooled CLIP ViT-L/14 patch tokens at 224. Head: logistic, C by inner cross-validation over persons, five seeds; arm (i) photos against uniform-0.5 morphs, arm (ii) photos, zero-field (warp-only) images and both halves against the same morphs; trained on the 530 training persons of the alpha-field probe (AF0), threshold at 5% false alarms on its validation genuine images. Reads on the landmark ladder (AR1), OpenCV-style engine deciding: (a) warp-only against two-person morph, AUC and excess over the best of 27 statistics; (b) warp-only softened to 61 px against the native two-person morph of the same 200 hosts; (c) paired shift from photo to its 61 px copy in standard deviations, and share flagged (112.7 px copies separately); (d) AUC on the Poisson set (H1); (e) EER on corrected MAD22 OpenCV and Webmorph, native and history-matched (FRLL-Morphs cells printed, not gated). About 4 CPU-hours. Tier 1 (decisive, Athena, about 5 A100-hours, one day after the softened set is complete): four ViT-B/16 LoRA fits with the unchanged training script (6,250 steps, last checkpoint, seeds 401 and 402); manifest A photos against morphs; manifest B photos, zero-field images, halves and their 61 px copies against morphs and their 61 px copies; same reads (a) to (e), no flip averaging.
cards.pass_and_kill: Pass (tier 1, manifest B, both seeds): (a) at least 0.95 with excess over the best statistic at least 0.03 and a lower bound above 0; (b) at least 0.90; (c) shift at most 0.3 standard deviations and at most 10% flagged; (d) at least 0.85 (measured bar 0.833 for the MADation-recipe ViT-L/14 retrains). Kill: (b) below 0.75, or the lower bound of the excess in (a) at or below 0, on both seeds; then the network reads softness at 224 and the landmark claim stops. Loss rule: the equality term is written only if manifest B passes (a) and (b) and fails (c); it stays only if it halves the shift and costs at most 0.02 on (a) and (b). Tier 0 can only warn: arm (ii) with (b) below 0.60 means frozen features hold no softness-free signal.
cards.compute: Tier 0: 0 GPU-hours, about 4 CPU-hours. Tier 1: about 5 A100-hours. Revised full plan: about 270 A100-hours (ViT-B/16 screen of 8 configurations at 3 seeds 26; frozen configuration at 5 seeds on ViT-L/14 18; eight ablation rows 140; three reference rows 53; scoring 30), against 830 in the original; the 3.5-hour ViT-L/14 fit time is an estimate.
cards.reason: It is the natural network for the paper and the reduced plan fits three days, but its table claim shrinks to a tie on easy cells and an open result on the clean MAD22 cells. The loss is known work, and whether a LoRA fit passes the crossed softness control is shown by nothing on disk.

cards.name: Canonical-band network at the smallest benchmark storage size
cards.one_line: Demoted from a candidate network to a measurement: a size sweep on frozen CLIP that shows where storage history stops being readable and what the morph head has lost by then, with one ablation arm of recipe 1 at that size only if the sweep passes.
cards.novelty: Found: Grommelt et al., 'Fake or JPEG?', size and JPEG biases in a detection benchmark (ECCVW 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17608), the closest statement of the problem. PW-MAD keeps only images with at least 90 px between the eyes (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10291, search summary). OrthoMAD includes a 64 by 64 low-resolution set (https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07841, search summary). Singh and Ramachandra study morph detection across camera resolutions, differential setting (IJCB 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.15474, search summary). Spreeuwers et al., EUSIPCO 2018, sensitivity to simple disguise techniques (found, details not verified). Our round 1 had 'one network at the common Nyquist'. Not found: a morph-detection paper that trains and tests at one small fixed face scale to remove storage history. NOT VERIFIED: the same idea in generated-image detection; the search budget ran out before I could look.
cards.strongest_objection: The promise 'storage history absent by construction' fails at the only band that matters: histories of 101 px and more are already invisible at 224 (the generator's own section 2.2), the ones that move detectors sit at 61 to 65 px, and a size near 150 puts the face at 63 to 67 px, the same band, where a thrice-filtered stored photo still differs from a once-resized one; and declaring softness 'evidence at a fixed size' is the behaviour the paper measures in the SelfMAD release and calls a failure.
cards.likeliest_confound: Softness at the chosen size: the Laplacian floor for morph against its halves rises as resolution falls (0.76 at 512, 0.87 at 224, measured), so a morph head at 0.95 near 150 px may be a band-power reader (expected, not measured). Control: the best single statistic computed on the same resized arrays, printed beside the history probe and beside the morph head, and the flag rate on blurred genuine photos.
cards.revised_design: Recipe 2 is no longer a candidate network; it becomes a measurement and, if it passes, one ablation arm of recipe 1. Frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 is run through timm directly at 224, 182, 154, 140, 126 and 112 px with resampled position embeddings, because the project's CLIP builder refuses any size other than 224 (archs_a12.py lines 36 to 37); the resize-down-and-up form is a blur made of two resizes and runs only with the author's explicit yes. At each size: a history probe (photo against its own stored copy, per pool and per kernel), the same contrast for the best single statistic, a cross-tool morph head (warp-only against two-person morph) and its excess over the best statistic. The resulting figure goes into the paper whatever the outcome. Only if a size passes: one ViT-B/16 arm of recipe 1 at that size, with and without the 61 px copies, five seeds, labelled 'input-side alternative', never 'by construction'. Softness is never called evidence, and the flag rate on blurred genuine photos is printed for every arm.
cards.first_test: Data, listed and present: face crops of FRLL photos and stored copies under /mnt/t7/smad_next/RS1/crops/{main,amend} (manifest sets G_raw, E7raw_mordiff, E7raw_dim_a, E7raw_greedy_dim, Gresample50_frll, 204 each); three-kernel history pools e7area, e7bicubic, e7lanczos for MorDIFF, DiM-A and Greedy-DiM under /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a46_corrective_20261108/rgb_clip/ (these are crops of SelfMAD crops, RS1 README 16:45; label them so); ladder crops /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/crops/main (18,245 files). NOT present: blur crops (the RS1 manifest has JPEG 50, JPEG 70 and the 50% shrink pool, no blur set); crop the existing blurred frames first or drop that read. Features: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14, mean-pooled tokens, six sizes; statistics (Laplacian variance, band-power set) on the same resized arrays. Head 1: logistic, photo against own stored copy, five folds by FRLL person (102), folded AUC with person bootstrap. Head 2: logistic, warp-only against two-person morph, trained on one engine and tested on the other. About 1 A100-hour and 2 CPU-hours, half a day.
cards.pass_and_kill: Pass: a size exists where, on every 61 to 65 px pool and all three kernels, head 1 is at most 0.60 (upper bound at most 0.65) and the best single statistic is at most 0.60, and head 2 is at least 0.95 with excess over the best statistic at least 0.03 (lower bound above 0). Kill as a network: no such size; or at the largest size that passes head 1 the excess of head 2 has a lower bound at or below 0; or more than 20% of blurred genuine photos are flagged there. The measurement is kept in either case.
cards.compute: Sweep: about 1 A100-hour plus 2 CPU-hours. If it passes: one ablation arm of 10 ViT-B/16 fits, about 11 A100-hours.
cards.reason: The cheap sweep is worth a figure and explains why SMDD-trained detectors live in the 61 to 65 px band. As a network the recipe gives invariance only where 224 already has it and makes softness its signal, which is the cue the paper attacks.

cards.name: SMDD-Ladder: three-family ladder built only from SMDD renders
cards.one_line: The comparable SMDD-only row and a releasable set: rebuilt landmark morphs with warped halves and warp-only images as genuine, plus diffusion-autoencoder rungs under policy A if a render-to-photo transfer test passes; no GAN family and no mirror rung in training.
cards.novelty: Found: SYN-MAD 2022, training limited to synthetic data (Huber et al., IJCB 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07337, abstract read); SynMorph, a synthetic morph set with 2,450 identities, over 100,000 morphs and mated samples (Zhang et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05595, abstract read; whether it has generator morphs or one-person rungs is NOT verified and it must be read in full before any 'new set' claim); DRCT (ICML 2024, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/chen24ay.html). From our record, not reopened by me: SMDD (arXiv 2203.06691), SelfMAD (arXiv 2504.05504), Aligned Datasets (arXiv 2410.11835), B-Free (2412.17671), Dual Data Alignment (2505.14359). Not confirmed: that Zhang et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09817) add GAN-reconstructed genuine images (abstract does not say). Remains new: one-render reconstructions as genuine beside two-render mixes of the same generator, on the standard training source, with every camera-photo ladder held out. Incremental.
cards.strongest_objection: Two of the three families teach a cue and the third has no softness control: all GAN rungs are StyleGAN2 output separated by latent position (unreviewed: latent averageness 0.9998, spread-matched renders score like morphs at 0.46 to 0.47, transfer to MIPGAN cells 0.38 to 0.73) while an SMDD-only network is taught that StyleGAN2 output is genuine, so the expected 2 to 8% on GAN cells has no support; the mirror rung is a symmetric face (asymmetry 2.1 against 12 to 19.6); and under the image rules SMDD has no softening strength between 20 px and its native 63 px.
cards.likeliest_confound: Diffusion rungs: sampler and noise statistics of the mixed latent, and PNG size (unreviewed: at 100 steps Laplacian variance alone gives 0.966 with morphs sharper than reconstructions, PNG size 0.73 to 0.80, statistics 0.66 to 0.70 at 20 steps; experiments/FZ1/result.md P4). Control: train at 20 steps, test at 100 steps and on published MorDIFF against reconstructions, and print the excess over PNG size. Landmark rungs: softness and SMDD's StyleGAN2 texture (cue matrix row 19); control: all camera-photo ladders unseen, read with the crossed softness contrast. Mirror rung: symmetry; control: keep it out of training.
cards.revised_design: Role: the comparable row (SMDD-only training) and a set to release, not the headline. Hosts are SMDD training-split genuine renders only. Landmark family: rebuilt morphs with balanced partners, both warped halves and warp-only images as genuine, no mirror rung in training. Diffusion family, only if the first test passes: the pinned diffusion autoencoder run unchanged on 6,000 renders, reconstruction counted as genuine (policy A), two-render mix as the morph, 20 steps with a 100-step subset. No GAN family. Backbone, crop, schedule, threshold rule and reports as in the revised recipe 1, with no order term. The paper states that SMDD allows no softening strength in the 61 to 95 px band and reads the storage and softness controls on camera-photo pools, all unseen. Ablation rows: released SMDD; rebuilt with balanced partners; plus halves and warp-only; plus diffusion rungs. Claim: at the level of published SMDD-trained rows on landmark cells with a lower fixed-threshold miss, weaker than the camera-photo row on the clean MAD22 cells, no claim on GAN cells. Release pair lists, code and derived images, shared with the SMDD authors as their terms ask.
cards.first_test: Part A (no generation). Data: the existing diffusion blocks of colorFERET and FRGC persons under /mnt/t7/smad_research/diffae-expanded123-v1/run/ (present; 130 entries listed, the recipe says 102 complete blocks, the paired-differences diffusion run counts 129; fix the list first); their CLIP features are those of that run under /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/diffae/ (path to confirm with its owner); FRLL arms of the earlier MorDIFF controls under /mnt/t7/smad_next/FZ1/feats/clip_mad (present). Features: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14, mean-pooled. Head: logistic, two-person morph against reconstruction of the same host, trained on the colorFERET and FRGC blocks. Reads on FRLL with person bootstrap: two-person morph against reconstruction at 20 steps and at 100 steps; published MorDIFF against reconstructions; reconstruction against camera photo; same-person mix against two-person morph (printed only); PNG size and Laplacian variance as floors. CPU, 2 to 3 hours. Part B (render to photo, 1 to 2 A100-hours after the generation gate of the Athena diffusion experiment (DG1) has passed): the diffusion autoencoder on 600 SMDD renders, 600 reconstructions and 300 two-render mixes at 20 steps; the same head trained on renders only; the same FRLL reads.
cards.pass_and_kill: Pass: two-person morph against reconstruction on FRLL at 20 steps at least 0.90 (lower bound at least 0.85); published MorDIFF against reconstructions at least 0.85; the 100-step read at least 0.80; excess over PNG size at least 0.10; reconstruction against camera photo at most 0.65. Kill the diffusion rungs: render-trained head below 0.80 at 20 steps; or the part A proxy below 0.85; or the 100-step read below 0.70 (the head then reads the step count); or reconstruction against camera photo above 0.65. If killed, the row is the landmark rebuild alone, which the SMDD audit (SM1) already builds (45,000 images in /mnt/t7/smad_next/SM1/img/armc).
cards.compute: Part A: 0 GPU-hours. Part B: 1 to 2 A100-hours. Full revised row: about 90 A100-hours (generation on 6,000 renders 25 to 40, A100 rate not measured; three rows at five seeds on ViT-L/14 about 53), against 150 in the original.
cards.reason: Reviewers will ask for an SMDD-only row and the landmark half is already on disk, so it is needed and reachable. Its GAN and mirror rungs teach cues, its landmark family has no softness control of its own, and render-to-photo transfer of the diffusion head is untested.

cards.name: Training with a false-alarm limit for every storage history
cards.one_line: Train the unchanged MADation recipe (CLIP with LoRA, low-rank adaptation) on crossed data with environment-balanced batches and a genuine-side margin, show a violation of the limit by the usual-loss arm first, and claim the joint result at one fixed rule (every left-out genuine pool at most 5% flagged AND far fewer missed AMSL and WebMorph morphs); the per-environment weight update is only an ablation arm.
cards.novelty: Opened by me (abstract pages only). Sagawa et al., ICLR 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.08731: worst-group training; a network that fits its training set has near-zero worst-group training loss, so the group objective alone changes nothing without strong regularisation. Cotter et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04198: rate constraints with multipliers, which is the proposed weight update. Tong, Feng, Li, Science Advances 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.03109: lowest miss under a false-alarm bound. Sun et al., CVPR 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13662: one classifier shared across domains in face anti-spoofing. Kashiani et al., IJCB 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10392: consistency regularisation in morph detection, no rate constraint on the abstract page. Ju et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16635: group-wise losses over demographic groups. What remains new as far as checked: a false-alarm limit per processing history as the training constraint in morph detection, proved on left-out histories, with the rule shipped with the network. NOT verified: a full search (the web-search budget ran out after two queries); the loss itself is known and must not be claimed.
cards.strongest_objection: The constraint is slack where it is applied. My UNREVIEWED reads of existing files in /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/EV1_fixed-threshold-reread/: the five ViT-L/14 recipe retrains (usual loss, SMDD only) flag 0.0% of all 23 genuine pools at their own rule and detect 0% of AMSL, 14 to 59% of WebMorph (AM2_B1_rule05.csv); at the development threshold they flag at most 4.9% of every full-frame shrink-history pool, but 23 to 50% of JPEG 50 photos and 43 to 76% of the tight MorDIFF frame (A1_false_alarms.csv); with a threshold from any shrink-history pool their miss on the four FRLL landmark cells is 0.00 (AM2_B3_miss_by_threshold_pool.csv). So there is no storage-history violation to remove on this recipe; its failures are JPEG (not trainable: no JPEG code allowed, no JPEG copy of a training photo exists), the frame (declared out of scope) and missed morphs at the fixed rule, which a false-alarm limit does not help. The history failure is real for the ViT-B/16 retrains (23 to 67% of DiM-history pools flagged). In a LoRA fit the training-pool flag rate reaches zero quickly, so the weights never rise.
cards.likeliest_confound: A score offset between capture domains: a network that puts every camera photo far below its rule passes 'every left-out genuine pool at most 5%' with no invariance (the SMDD-trained recipe does this: 0% flags, 0% of AMSL detected). Control: always print the pair (flag rate, miss) at the same rule and require the usual-loss arm to violate the limit first. Second, for the head test: a softness window (the two registered doses roughly bracket the morph on whole-frame Laplacian variance; my arithmetic, not measured as such). Control: 61.2 px copies of ladder R4 morphs must still be flagged, and corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher is read against its own history-matched photos.
cards.revised_design: The method is the crossed data (SMDD rebuild arms plus FRGC and colorFERET landmark material, no FRLL, FFHQ or FEI person), environment-balanced batches and a fixed genuine-side margin on the unchanged recipe; the per-environment weight update is an ablation arm, kept only if it beats balanced batches. A violation is shown first: the usual-loss arm on the same data must exceed the limit in a left-out environment, otherwise the constraint is reported as not needed. The storage-history claim is tested on the ViT-B/16 recipe, where the failure is measured; the ViT-L/14 network is the headline and must keep its landmark numbers. Environments exist on both sides: genuine pool by state, and morph tool by state (as built; morph then shrink at 112.7 and 61.2 px). The frame becomes an environment: the same constant-colour blanking in the tight-frame geometry for genuine images and morphs, because the tight frame is the pool that binds. JPEG rows are printed as uncontrolled until the author rules on the registered JPEG branch. Training length, early stop or weight decay and the seed list are fixed in advance and every seed is printed. Two operating points are printed for every detector: own rule and the development 5% threshold. The claim is joint: every left-out genuine pool at most 5% flagged and miss on AMSL and WebMorph at the same rule far below the SMDD-trained recipe (100% and 41 to 86% missed at its own rule, unreviewed). The border-free read is corrected MAD22 OpenCV and Webmorph, whose morph files have the photos' size. Diffusion and GAN cells are printed under both class policies with no claim that the limit creates signal.
cards.first_test: Fixed-rule head test, revised (NU1r). cards.name: Train only on what the measured cues cannot explain
cards.one_line: Use the audited cue model as an acceptance test for training sets (out-of-fold AUC at most 0.90 with enough mixed images) and as clipped inverse weights that make label and cues independent; keep the logit-offset fit only as a comparison arm and report a per-cell price column.
cards.novelty: Opened by me (abstract pages only). Clark, Yatskar, Zettlemoyer, EMNLP 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.03683: bias-only model ensembled with the main model in training; this is the proposed loss. He, Zha, Wang, 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10763: fit the residual of a biased model built from known bias features. Bahng et al., ICML 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02806: the vision version, be different from a model biased by design. Puli et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00520 and Makar et al., AISTATS 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.06422: make label and nuisance independent with known nuisance labels (covers the overlap-weights arm). Grommelt et al., 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17608: closest in image forensics, measured JPEG and size cues removed at the data level, more than 11 points better across generators. What remains new: the bias model taken from a measured audit of a morph benchmark, and the cue model's AUC as an acceptance rule for a training set. NOT verified: whether this loss with hand-made cue features exists in forensics or morph detection (search did not run); RUBi not opened.
cards.strongest_objection: The 'by construction' claim is wrong: the loss is minimised by f(x) = log-odds(label given image) minus b(x), so wherever the image says more than the cues (our heads reach 0.98 to 1.00 on the ladder) the detector learns to subtract the cue model and at test time scores soft genuine images lower and sharp morphs higher; the price falls on soft morphs, and morph files are stored small in 8 of 17 cells. Also: blending itself lowers band power and one band-power number gives 0.912 for warp-only against two-person morphs (PD1 landmark result.md, unreviewed, one fold), so boosted trees on 27 statistics will pass the idea's own 0.95 overlap limit and the first test is inadmissible as written; columns defined only for morphs (tool, partner) saturate the offset; the cue model is global while a network can read local softness.
cards.likeliest_confound: Over-correction: 'history-matched pools at most 10% flagged' and 'absolute cue correlation at most 0.2' are met by a head that learned 'soft means less morph-like'. Control: report the signed correlation and make the soft-against-soft rows mandatory (corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher against its history-matched photos, both in the bench_s list, and 61.2 px copies of ladder R4); the error there must not rise against the usual fit. Also: 'two-person against same-person is softness-matched' rests on PNG size alone (0.508); the same file gives 0.616 folded for a 32-pixel thumbnail and 0.587 for background statistics (experiments/AR1/baselines.json, unreviewed), so the full 27-statistic floor must be printed for that rung.
cards.revised_design: The cue model becomes an acceptance test for any training set: boosted trees on the 27 statistics, the colour statistics and the border share, fitted out of fold by person, with no column that exists for one class only. Acceptance is out-of-fold AUC at most 0.90 and at least 150 images per class with absolute log-odds below 2; otherwise the set is crossed further before any fit, which replaces the one-number Laplacian rule. The method arm is the usual loss with clipped inverse weights 1 / p(label given cues), whose optimum has no minus-b term. The logit-offset fit is a comparison arm only. Signed cue correlation is reported, never the absolute value alone. The soft-against-soft rows are mandatory. Its role in the paper is a price column per cell (error with cue-balanced weights minus error with the usual loss); no state-of-the-art claim rests on it. Leaving one cue family out stays, to state how far the protection reaches. The LoRA stage (one ViT-B/16 pair) runs only if the head test passes.
cards.first_test: Cue-balance test, revised (NU2r), no GPU. Step A, admissibility (about 20 CPU-minutes): cue model for R4 against R0 and R2w, OpenCV-style engine, 536 hosts, 5 partner-safe folds by person, cues from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/ar1.npz (exists; 26 statistics and PNG size); report out-of-fold AUC and the count of images per class with absolute log-odds below 2. Step B, only if admissible: features /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/landmark/feat/dinov3_512/af0_ar1_mean.npz and af0_bench_s_mean.npz (both exist; DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512, mean patch token), cues /mnt/t7/smad_next/AF0/cues/bench_s.npz (exists); three logistic heads: usual, inverse-weighted, logit offset. Metrics on held-out hosts and bench_s: signed rank correlation of the score with the cue log-odds among FRLL genuine photos; flag rate on each landmark history pool at the threshold flagging 5% of native FRLL photos; EER on MAD22 FaceMorpher against its history-matched pool; EER on the seven landmark cells; AUC of R3 against R4. Under 1 CPU-hour, 1 to 2 hours wall.
cards.pass_and_kill: Pass: Step A admissible; the weighted head halves the worst history-pool flag rate or brings it to 10% or less; signed correlation within plus or minus 0.2; MAD22 FaceMorpher against its history-matched pool at most 2 points above the usual head; family-mean EER on the seven cells within 3 points of the usual head. Kill as a method (keep the acceptance rule): Step A gives AUC above 0.95 or fewer than 150 mixed images per class and softened morphs are not built by the evening of 12 Nov. Kill the offset arm: signed correlation below minus 0.2. Kill the weighted arm: landmark EER up by more than 5 points with no fall in history-pool flags. If the usual head is already at 10% or less on every history pool the head test says nothing and one ViT-B/16 LoRA pair decides.
cards.compute: First test: 0 GPU-hours, under 1 CPU-hour. If it passes: cue statistics for the training images (generator's estimate about 8 core-hours, not verified; Athena is GPU-only so this runs on the saturated DGX) and one ViT-B/16 pair, about 2.2 A100-hours.
cards.reason: The acceptance rule and the price column are worth having, but the loss is known and its optimum subtracts the cue model, which is not what the write-up claims. It protects against listed whole-frame cues only, and the data it needs (softened morphs, a dose grid, cue statistics for 100,000 images) do not exist yet.

cards.name: Canonical view: one storage band and frame for every input
cards.one_line: Dropped as a method: the band removes a cue the leading recipe does not use and leaves the ones the record shows at work; the common frame mask moves into the main protocol and the band-matched read already exists as columns.
cards.novelty: Not searched (budget used up). Verified neighbour: Grommelt et al., 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17608 (equalising JPEG and size cues at the data level). From the repository's own class-definition check, not re-opened by me: Scherhag et al. 2020 give both classes the same post-processing. From memory, NOT verified: detectors built on 112-pixel face-recognition crops are band-limited by design; fixed input transformations are a known defence in adversarial robustness. A fixed degradation of every test input as part of a morph detector was not found by me, but I did not look. The frame mask is already on the table (cue table row 7; EV1 review follow-up 3).
cards.strongest_objection: For the eight cells 'already at the band' the canonical view is the identity on the morph and the existing history control on the photo (prep_eval.py lines 119 to 125: the call shrinks only if the scale is below 1). That comparison is in the record: a ViT-B/16 network that never saw a morph still reaches 0.55% EER on corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher and 5.25% on MorDIFF against history-matched photos (/home/narolski/mambamorph-code/smadcvpr/results/A47/a47_read.md, reviewed earlier). Certificate part b cannot hold because the path cannot restore detail (a render at 63 px against its copy at 20 px stays separable). 'A history above the band is not in the input' is empirical, and the ViT-B/16 retrains react to a 112.7 px history through a 224 input (unreviewed read of A1_false_alarms.csv). The ViT-L/14 recipe shows no shrink-history failure (0 to 4.9% flagged; AUC 0.999 to 1.000 in every crossed landmark cell). The front end treats inputs differently by native resolution, which collides with 'no gate on resolution', and a 61 px band is below the reported passport minimum.
cards.likeliest_confound: Read (c), EER at most 5% on MAD22 FaceMorpher at the band, is passed by a network with no morph in training (0.55%): the route into the band, the pasted surround and the visible vendor watermark in those files (AF0 README section 8) are enough. Control: print the morph-free network as a row of read (c) and blank the surround and the bottom band in both classes. Read (a) passes trivially because both arms end with the same box filter.
cards.first_test: Check that confirms the drop or revives the idea, existing files only. Route check: the 204 stored-small photos (arm E of the MorDIFF ladder study, A43; manifest /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a43/data/manifests/a43.csv, exists) against the history-matched MorDIFF frames of the same photos (eval.csv, set mordiff, variant resmatch, 204 rows counted): same persons, same tight frame, same band (median IED 65.07 and 65.14 px, border 0.543 and 0.545 in EV1 AM2.json). Features: DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512 and CLIP ViT-L/14 at 224, mean patch token (408 frames to extract); head: logistic probe, 5 folds by person; metric: probe AUC with a person-bootstrap interval. Beside it, already in a47_read.md: the morph-free network against history-matched photos on the eight band cells. About 0.1 GPU-hours, minutes of CPU, 1 to 2 hours wall.
cards.pass_and_kill: Revive only if the route probe is at most 0.55 (upper bound at most 0.60) on both features AND the morph-free network is at 40% EER or more on MAD22 FaceMorpher once surround and watermark are blanked in both classes. Otherwise the drop stands. I expect it to stand (the SelfMAD release flags 97% of the stored-small pool against 79% of the history-matched pool, EV1 review).
cards.compute: Check: about 0.1 GPU-hours and minutes of CPU. The dropped method would have needed about 45 A100-hours plus about 28 core-hours on a saturated CPU machine (generator's estimates).
cards.reason: Removal from the input is the strongest kind of protection, but here it removes a cue the leading recipe does not use and leaves the route, generator trace, JPEG and frame cues that the record shows at work. The method needs a new test-time scope, an author ruling on the resolution branch and a large CPU build, for an expected loss on AMSL and WebMorph.

vetting.cross_cutting: All three ideas aim at storage history, but in existing score files the ViT-L/14 recipe retrains show no such failure: 0.0% of 23 genuine pools flagged at their own rule with 0% of AMSL detected, at most 4.9% of any full-frame shrink-history pool at the development threshold, against 23 to 50% for JPEG 50 and 43 to 76% for the tight MorDIFF frame (my UNREVIEWED reads of AM2_B1_rule05.csv and A1_false_alarms.csv in the fixed-threshold re-read, EV1); storage history is a ViT-B/16 and SelfMAD result, so the lens should be re-aimed at JPEG, the frame and missed morphs at a fixed rule. A fixed-rule table must always print flag rate and miss together, because a flag rate alone rewards a detector that never fires. No softened copy of a ladder morph exists; one CPU job (61.2 and 112.7 px copies of the 536 OpenCV-style R4 morphs) serves the first tests of ideas 1 and 2 and the soft-against-soft control. JPEG cannot enter training under the allowed list; the registered function that holds the approved shrink branch also holds JPEG, blur and 50% resample branches, and running them unchanged on training images needs the author's yes. Corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher is not usable as evidence of morph detection without blanking (watermark, surround, and a morph-free network at 0.55% EER under the history control). Two-person against same-person morphs is not yet a softness-free contrast (thumbnail 0.616 folded in AR1 baselines.json). Head tests on frozen pooled features have little room (3 to 6% flagged in AF0 cn0.json), so each first test names the condition under which a ViT-B/16 LoRA pair decides instead. The novelty check is incomplete: the web-search budget ran out after two queries, and prior work rests on 13 arXiv abstract pages opened directly.
